# Grey Retention MVP — Build Ledger

This file is the durable cross-task memory. Every implementation task must update only its own row and append a handoff entry. Never mark an item complete without verification evidence.

## Blocked, needs Raman

Work that waits for the owner's decision or OK (master handoff: ask Raman only for these). Each line says what is waiting and what happens after the OK. The rest of the queue goes on meanwhile.

- **The first real Klaviyo call** (LRN-001, PSH-001). Everything is built and tested against Klaviyo's published API, behind `KLAVIYO_MODE=live` and `KLAVIYO_DRAFT_PUSH=live` (both off). Asked: one read-only call to a real account, to confirm the report and click ids LRN-001 reads; then the first real draft (PSH-001's list of things to check is in its handoff).
- **The Meta Ad Library route** (ONB-104). The live reader needs Meta's official Ad Library API (an app and a token: a new service), or the owner's own ad account later. Until then a synthetic brand reads sample ads and a real brand's ads are not read.
- **Privacy policy and terms** (section 8, POLICY-DRAFT). Drafts are written from the app's real data flows, at `/privacy` and `/terms`, shown only with `LEGAL_DRAFTS=on`, never indexed and not linked from sign-up. Asked: every field in `docs/legal/CHECKLIST.md`, first **the legal entity and its registered address** (not confirmed: no entity or address is published until it is). After the OK: the fields filled, a lawyer's review if wanted, then the sign-up link.
- **Deleting an account or a whole workspace** (section 8). The server side can be built; what is kept (results, drafts in Klaviyo) and how long, and every real deletion, wait for Raman.
- **The hosted project's sign-in limits** (BAS-004). They are set in its Supabase dashboard, which touching needs Raman's OK (or Raman checks Authentication → Rate Limits there).
- **Frequency caps and overlap for segments** (SEG-EXPOSURE-001, PROJECT_TODOS: owner decisions and design required). The frequency window and cap per person, which segment wins an overlap, priorities, and how sends made outside the app count. Asked: those rules (VISION's 30 to 35 campaigns a month and about 12 per person are examples, not caps). After the OK: the exposure checks, then PLAN-SEG-001 carries audiences through the plan. The segment rules themselves (SEG-STRATEGY-001) are built.
- **Grow the inbox fast** (owner pick #45: sign up 200+ brands per industry with plus-addresses). Signing up to real brands' newsletters is an outside action in the owner's name, from the inbox Gmail account. Asked: an OK to sign up, which industries first, and whether a person or the app fills the sign-up forms. After the OK: a per-industry brand list with one plus-address each (`features/inbox/addresses.ts`) and a sign-up tracker. The emails that arrive already flow through INB-001 to 004.
- **Picture work in the design studio** (owner picks #4 product cut-outs, #12 smart crop, and #15 dark-mode-safe pictures, which needs #4's cut-outs). Removing a product photo's background and finding the product or a face in a photo need an image model or service: a new paid service, or paid AI beyond the Gemini cap. Asked: which service, if any, or to leave them until the design studio is turned on (`DESIGN_STUDIO`, off). Until then a designed section places the store's photos as they are.
- **Tagging quality and the Step 1 gate** (CI-001, CI-002). Real section tags need paid Gemini and 50 sections labelled by a person to compare against (the gate: 85% agreement). Asked: an OK for that paid AI run and who labels the 50. Until then tagging runs on the fake AI.
- **Findings only a model can give** (ONB-101, ONB-105, ONB-106c). The Site reader's tone and audience, review themes, and the Brand strategist's own summary need a live AI model on real pages. Asked: an OK to switch the readers' AI on for one test brand (paid AI). Until then the facts come from code rules and the samples.
- **The first live catalog read** (ONB-102, with `KLAVIYO_MODE=live`). Shopify's property names and the 200-order payload are checked against Klaviyo's published shapes only. Asked: watching one real catalog read with Raman's OK.
- **Price-check thresholds and the EU "carbon neutral" claim rule** (ONB-063, ONB-062). The price bands need tuning on real catalogs, and whether "carbon neutral" is refused for EU stores is a legal call. Asked: Raman's rule for both.
- **Screens that need a design first** (master handoff design rule). The Brand book review page (#58), the logo and photo-library screens, and a competitors step beyond Follow and Hide. Asked: approved designs. The data layers are built.
- **Which lane builds ONB-106c/d and LRN-002** (BUILD_BRIEF section 5 gives them to lane A; MASTER_HANDOFF phases 7 and 8 give them to lane B). Asked: who owns them. Until then neither lane starts them, and the lanes keep coordinating through this ledger.
- **`.env.example` is out of date** (ONB-102, KLV-001): `KLAVIYO_API_REVISION`, the missing `KLAVIYO_MODE`, and `KLAVIYO_WRITE_LOCK` (KLV-LOCK: absent means locked; it should be listed absent or as `locked`, never `unlocked`). Coding sessions may not read `.env*` files, so Raman, or a session he allows, updates the placeholder file.
- **Model shutdown dates** (owner pick #83). The model retirement watch is built, but no date is filled in: build sessions cannot reach the providers' deprecation pages. Asked: allow `ai.google.dev` and `platform.openai.com` in the build environment's network settings (or paste the dates). After the OK: each model's line in `lib/providers/model-retirements.ts` gets its date, and the admin Operations page warns six weeks ahead.
- ~~**Which lane builds ONB-106c/d and LRN-002**~~ Decided by Raman on 24 Nov 2026: the cloud session that fixed the Gemini models (AI-MDL-001) builds them, ONB-106c first (see its row).
- **`.env.example` is out of date** (ONB-102, KLV-001): `KLAVIYO_API_REVISION` and the missing `KLAVIYO_MODE`. Coding sessions may not read `.env*` files, so Raman, or a session he allows, updates the placeholder file.
- **Model shutdown dates** (owner pick #83). The Gemini dates are filled in (AI-MDL-001, read from Google's deprecations page on 24 Nov 2026). The OpenAI lines still wait: `platform.openai.com` was not read. Asked: allow it in the build environment's network settings (or paste the dates). After the OK: the two OpenAI lines in `lib/providers/model-retirements.ts` get their dates.
- **A paid Gemini key** (AI-MDL-001). The first live run (24 Nov 2026, on a key the owner lent for this test only) was on Google's free tier: 20 calls a day per model, about two emails. Asked: billing on for the key's project in Google AI Studio, then one more run of the 10 golden emails with every agent (the run's script is described in AI-MDL-001's handoff). Until then the new defaults are proved by tests, not by a live run.

## Optional later

Not blocking anything: built without it, and it would add to what already works. Kept here so it is not forgotten.

- **Instagram captions for the founder's voice** (owner pick #23). Verified 20 Nov 2026 (FOUNDER-VOICE, PIC-23g): the voice is learned from the owner's own sent emails alone, and the Letter writer uses it, end to end on fixtures. Captions would add more of the founder's words; they need Meta's Instagram API (an app, a review and the owner's Instagram business account connected: a new service). The `SocialSource` port is kept for it.

## Global decisions

- PLN-040b (27 Nov 2026): **the ladder remembers the sale.** `PlanInput.existing[].percent` is now filled, only from GROS's own knowledge, never from Klaviyo's words: `readOfferPercents(db, tenantId, { campaignIds, live })` (`features/strategy/offer-memory.ts`, worker client, every read `eq tenant_id`) takes the newest `drafted` `email_builds` row of each Klaviyo campaign in the plan's existing window (`windowCampaigns`, `sample_draft` = not live), its `email.code` and `email.offer.percent`; for a build older than REL-OFF's `offer`, the planned slot's offer (`strategy_runs.plan->slots[slot].offer`) when it names the same code. A draft with no code gives nothing; a draft the owner edited in Klaviyo (PICK-99: `klaviyo_email_results.changed` or `design_changed`, read by `tenant_id` and build) is never evidence: no percent, and its `offer` flag stays Klaviyo's. `planFromHistory(history, window, percents)` marks such a send `offer: true` with its `percent` in `existing` (7 days back, as before) and lists the known ones from `saleLookbackDays` (14) back in the new optional `PlanInput.saleOffers` (`{ date, percent }`), which only the ladder reads: the cap, offer share and spacing checks never see it. A failed read is logged and plans as before. The sale window: `saleGapDays` = 14 (two offer spacings); `carriedSalePercent(known, firstOfferDay)` is the latest known-percent offer email before the plan's first offer email, at most 14 days before it, also one on or after the plan's first day (a plan starts tomorrow, and the last offer email is often scheduled then); the highest percent that day; else null. `ladderStart` (over `existing` and `saleOffers`) starts the ladder there, clamped to the biggest allowed code that still works (so never above the max discount or the margin floor's cap), else 10%, and returns the carry it used; `withOfferLadder` returns it as `carried`, and `saleNote(carried, slots)` adds one plain plan note from it when the sale goes on above 10%. `ladderStepsDown` is still not called by the plan.

- PICK-WIRE-PLAN (26 Nov 2026): **the 15-day plan reads its guidance** (owner picks #33, #37, #40, #48, #49). `PlanInput` gains optional `guidance` (`PlanGuidance`: `goals` from `goalProgress` for each month the window touches, `mix` from `emailMix` with `maxOffers` = `offersThatFit` (the offer share in whole emails over two weeks, at most one per spacing, none without offers), `competitors`: dated facts `competitor-times:<n>` / `competitor-offers:<n>` from `sendTimeMap` and `offerTracker` over the followed brands, never their codes), checked by `readPlanInput`. `planGuidance(db, …)` (`features/strategy/guidance.ts`) reads it with the worker's client for the claimed run's workspace only; each part is left out (logged) when unreadable and the plan step never fails for it (`runStrategyRuns` dep `guidance`). The competitor facts join `planEvidence`, so the Brief writer may cite them and slots show them as evidence; the Brief writer gets `revenue_goal` and the Calendar planner `email_mix` and `revenue_goal` (both prompts `2026-11-26.1`). Code still has the final word: after the last drop pass `withOfferLadder` gives every offer email its code from `offerLadder` (start at the smallest allowed code of at least 10%, step up, never down, never above the capped max), drops an offer email no code can hold and re-runs `keepPassing`; an offer fact on a slot names the code it carries. The code calendar types its plain emails by the mix (story without one, as before). `FifteenDayPlan` / `storedPlan` gain optional `goal` (`month`, `label`, `sentence`, `plan`, `pace`; a broken one reads as none), shown on Plan's "Revenue goal" card; the learned mix and the followed brands are plan notes. `mixKindOf` is exported from `features/results/mix.ts`.

- PICK-99 (26 Nov 2026, with the review fixes): **draft status sync extends LRN-001, never a second sync.** `klaviyo_email_results` gains `scheduled_for`, `send_strategy` (kept only while scheduled or sending; cleared by `save_klaviyo_result` otherwise; a table check on each), `design_changed` (sticky, like `changed`) and `design_evidence` (`{ variation, recorded, current, firstSeenAt, lastSeenAt, checks }`). "Edited in Klaviyo" = `changed` (subject, preview, campaign) or `design_changed`. A design difference is a variation's template HTML no longer matching the fingerprint PSH-001 stored in `klaviyo_draft_pushes.shown`, or another template on it; a first sight is only evidence, and `design_changed` is set only when a later, separate check sees the same difference (the database refuses it without stored evidence). Unknown, never "edited": a `:w` (write under way) entry, a push whose `shown` changed while we looked, a template 404, a variation with no template, nothing recorded. A check that finds the design as left clears unconfirmed evidence. A platform operator clears a change seen in error with `clear_klaviyo_design_change(build, reason)` (`features/results/design-clear.ts`; recorded in `workspace_events` as `klaviyo_design_change_cleared` with who, why and the evidence; no screen yet). The pusher's `shownOf`/`shownText`/`stillOurs` moved to `features/klaviyo-push/shown.ts` (behaviour unchanged). The hourly run reads templates only for draft/scheduled/sending (and once when first seen sent), never again once edited, 400 ms apart (Klaviyo's templates limit is one per account, shared with the push and the history read), inside the run's time; an account failure (pace, key, outage) pauses the account as before. **The email page never waits for Klaviyo:** it shows what was stored (with when it was last checked) and runs `checkEmailForPage` after its response (`after`, `checkEmailSoon`): service-only `claim_klaviyo_result(t, build, fresh)` (one row, 1-minute lease, only draft/scheduled/sending, not checked in 10 minutes, never while paused before its `next_check_at`, never while the hourly lease is live), its own client (2 s per request), the whole check raced to 4 s. **Never overwrite:** the live pusher reads the draft itself and refuses (`not_a_draft`, `externally_modified`, unchanged); `runEmailBuilds` also refuses before any pusher is called when the sync saw any draft of the same push key edited, scheduled, sending/sent, deleted or cancelled (`storedRefusal`, injectable `klaviyoState`; a failed read retries the step). That stored-state guard is forward-looking: today a drafted build is never pushed again (its key is re-pushed only from a failed build, which the sync never adopted), so it is defence for any later re-push path. New refusal codes `klaviyo_refused_{edited,scheduled,sent,deleted,cancelled}_in_klaviyo`; `externally_modified` and `not_a_draft` now say the same plain sentence ("…so GROS will not replace it. Plan next 15 days to make a new email instead."). Times: store time, the year shown when not this year; a `*local_timezone` send is wall-clock (read in UTC) and said "in each person’s own time zone". Shared read contracts gained fields: `EmailResult.designChanged/scheduledFor/sendStrategy`, `ResultLine.edited/scheduledFor/sendStrategy` (its "(changed in Klaviyo)" text is now "(edited in Klaviyo)"), `EmailBuildView.klaviyo?`, plan `in_klaviyo` status `words?`, `SentEmail.edited?` (learning: an edited send is never evidence nor counted toward any rule's three sends, nor toward retiring one; its top section is not learned), `EmailScreen.inKlaviyo` (with `checked`). Status pills stay BRAND.md's four: In Klaviyo for draft/scheduled/sending/sent/cancelled; no pill for deleted or never sent.
- PICK-101 (27 Nov 2026, with the review fixes): **list hygiene is one rule, as data, and it never holds an email back: when in doubt it keeps people.** `features/audiences/hygiene.ts` (pure): `hygieneRule(settings)` gives `{ version: 1, enabled, days (30 to 730, default 180), recentOrderDays = max(days, 180), minEmails = 5, countPrivacyOpens, engagedBy: click/open/site_visit/order, alwaysOut: hard_bounce, invalid_email, spam_complaint, unsubscribed, user_suppressed }`; `judge(facts, rule, now)` in this order: suppressed is out (`bounced` for a hard bounce or invalid email, else `suppressed`; even with hygiene off, never reachable); off keeps everyone else; an order in `recentOrderDays` keeps; a click, an open or a site visit in `days` keeps; **unknown is not unengaged** (clicks, opens, orders, the first email or the emails unknown keep, `unknown`; only site visits may be missing for a whole store, which keeps nobody); no email before the window keeps (`new`); fewer than 5 emails in the window keeps; else out, `unengaged`. **Apple Mail privacy opens (S4):** leaving them out is built (`countPrivacyOpens: false` and the segment's `Apple Privacy Open` metric filter) but **off**: `privacyOpenFilterProven = false`, so every open counts until that property is proven on a live account (it keeps more people). The owner reads "no clicks, opens, site visits or orders in 180 days". `countHygiene(groups)` counts each person once (bounced before unengaged), `reachable + leftOut = total`; the sample store reads "850 people left out: 310 bounced, 540 with no clicks, opens, site visits or orders in 180 days". Read-port types `LastSeen`, `Suppression`, `ProfileFacts`, `ProfileGroup` and the optional `KlaviyoSnapshot.profileGroups`.
  **The segment** (`lib/providers/klaviyo/hygiene-segment.ts`, pure): built only here, from typed inputs (`HygieneSegmentSpec`: days, recent-order days, minimum emails, the privacy filter flag, and metric ids); `hygieneSpec(rule, metrics)` makes none (`no_data`) when the metrics read is incomplete (`metrics_unread`), Klaviyo's Received, Clicked or Opened Email is missing (`no_email_metrics`) or the account has **no Placed Order metric** (`no_order_metric`): a keep-signal GROS cannot see never widens it. Every group must hold: Received Email at least once before the window and at least 5 times inside it (flow emails count too: the definition cannot tell campaigns from flows, and the card says so); Clicked Email 0; Opened Email 0; **one `equals 0` group per Active on Site metric and per Placed Order metric, whichever integration sends them** (Active on Site usually comes through `API`). **White label:** the name is `List hygiene · 180 days · v1 · <8-hex fingerprint of every input>`, never the product's name; other metrics give another name and another segment, and drafts switch to it. **The fence (KLV-LOCK-001, shared contract):** `isHygieneSegmentCreate` lets a `POST /api/segments` through only with that name pattern, `is_starred: false` and a definition shaped exactly as built (5 to 24 one-condition `profile-metric` count groups, `equals 0` or `at least 1–100`, `in-the-last`/`before` 30 to 730 days, no filter but the exact Apple one); still refused while locked; no segment is ever changed or deleted (docs/KLAVIYO_WRITE_LOCK.md). `lib/providers/klaviyo/segments.ts`: `readAccountId`, `readHygieneMetrics`, `findSegmentsByName`, `readSegment` (definition and size), `createHygieneSegment(spec)`; fake `recorded-segments.ts`.
  **The push** (`features/klaviyo-push/hygiene.ts` `hygieneExclusion`, in the live pusher before the campaign is made, under the build's push lease): reads the account and the metrics; a stored ready segment is reused only for the same account and fingerprint and only after `readSegment` shows it still there (its size is kept); else a segment with the exact name is adopted only when `sameDefinition` (key order and a missing `metric_filters` ignored), one with our name and other rules is never used (`failed`, `name_taken`); else the claim is entered and the segment made. **Every error gives a draft that leaves nobody out** plus a stored reason (`refused`, `missing_scope`, `bad_key`, `write_locked` retried after a day; `klaviyo_unavailable`, `rate_limited`, `metrics_unread`, `error` after an hour); only the push's own time running out (`TimeUp`) is thrown on, and another push holding the claim (`HygieneBusy`, PT409) makes the push wait a moment. A ready row is never overwritten by an error. If Klaviyo refuses the campaign with the exclusion, it is made once more without it (`exclusionRefused`, `draft_refused`). **Deleted in Klaviyo:** a stored segment that is gone is `deleted` and not made again until the owner presses "Make it again" on Audiences (`retry_list_hygiene`); making it again silently would undo his choice. A draft already made is never changed.
  **Database:** one row per rule (`v1-180`) with `klaviyo_account_id`, `fingerprint`, the segment id and state (`creating`, `ready`, `no_data`, `failed`, `deleted`); `save_hygiene_segment` locks the tenant, then the build, then the row; a first save inserts the whole row in one statement (`on conflict do nothing`), then reads it `for update` and judges the claim again, so two first saves at once give one row and PT409 (checked with two live sessions), never 23505; entering `creating` stamps `create_started_at = now()` and the claimant and clears the old reason (the caller never sends a time); while a claim is under two minutes old only its claimant writes the row; after that anyone may take it over; `creating` is refused for a ready row of the same account and fingerprint. **Screen:** Audiences gets a "Left out" card (shown once Klaviyo is connected): the number, the sentence, where it comes from, the rule in three short lines; the owner saves the days (on or off stays as it is) or turns it on or off (`saveListHygiene`, owner only; `set_list_hygiene` checks again with the page's revision) and, when the segment was deleted or failed, presses "Make it again" (`retryListHygiene`). Change history kind `list_hygiene_changed`. The exposure caps (SEG-EXPOSURE-001) are untouched.
- PICK-97 (27 Nov 2026, with the review fixes): **best send time per segment, counted in code from the history read (ONB-103), never a second Klaviyo report.** The history read also reads the sent campaigns' audiences (`readCampaignAudiences`: `filter=equals(messages.channel,'email'),any(id,[…])`, 100 ids a question, Klaviyo's next pages followed (at most 10 a question; no `page[size]`, which listing campaigns does not take); an extra: a failure or a partial read is logged and leaves those campaigns' sends to the store row only) and `features/onboarding/history/send-times.ts` (`sendTimes`, pure) counts per local hour and weekday in the store's timezone (DST-safe, `sendParts`). **Hours are only compared between sends to the same people:** an audience's own row counts only emails sent to that audience alone (one sent to several lists and segments counts for none of them: `facts.shared`); the store's row (`*`) compares hours within its most-sent audience set (`facts.within`; a known set with 3+ sends before sends whose audiences were not read). Left out (`leftOut`): Klaviyo-picked per-person times, under 100 recipients, no results, under 48 hours old. A send at each person's own clock time counts by that clock hour (the planner suggests a clock time too; that is the hour its people saw it). Engagement per recipient = (10 × unique clicks + unique opens − flagged machine opens) / recipients, summed per slot; Klaviyo's report flags no Apple privacy opens, so `machineOpens` is null today and clicks carry the weight. A recommendation needs 3 counted sends and an hour (weekday) sent to at least twice inside 07:00–21:00; else `reason` `few_sends` / `no_repeated_time` / `out_of_hours` ("not enough history"). `rivals` = other hours tried enough; `compared` (a clear winner) only when the best beat every rival by 10% (`minMargin`); strength `clear` / `close` ("did best so far") / `only`. Counts up to 10^15. Facts are kept apart from the recommendation in `klaviyo_send_times` (one row per workspace and audience; members read; only `record_send_times(job, lease, timezone, times)` writes, under the history job's lease, before `record_klaviyo_history`; the timezone must be the workspace's own (`tenants.timezone`); it replaces an older read's rows, never a newer one's, a newer stored (ready/empty) history counting too, the larger id winning a tie of `created_at`). The planner (`PlanInput.sendTimes?`, `features/strategy/send-times.ts`): `resolveSendTimes` gives each audience its own time, else the store's (never the store's weekday as the audience's), else the usual hour, else 10:00 — and **null when nothing was counted yet** (no rows, another timezone, the other live/sample kind, older than 30 days, unreadable): then no time is changed or explained. `withSendTimes` (in `planOutput`, both plans) sets each kept slot's time after the calendar rules, whatever an agent wrote, and keeps two emails on one day 3 hours apart (any audiences); the stronger reason keeps its hour (segment clear, close, only, then store, usual, default), then the earlier time. The Calendar planner (version bumped past both branches) gets `send_times` for `segment` and `store` rows only, with their basis, and `opens_most_on` only for an audience's own weekday. A planned slot carries `timing { basis, strength, othersTried, best, moved }` (stored plan: optional, an odd one is dropped); the Plan row's words claim only what the history shows ("9:00 am — when this group opens and clicks most", "the time that did best so far for this group", "the only time this group has had more than once", "…your store’s best hour so far", "moved from …"). The sample store has no send times: its plan is as before. GROS still never schedules (D17). PR #673 follow-up: `EmailResult.designEvidence` (stored `design_evidence`, not yet confirmed) counts as an owner edit in `sentEmail` (learning).

The Performance analyst's new dimension `spam_complaints`: a kind of email with at least `minSends` counted sends, `minSpamComplaints` (3) complaints and complaints at or over `spamComplaintRate` (1 in 1,000 people, the rate inbox providers start to warn at) is a "don't" for the planners, judged on its own rate (not against the rest), and is never a "do"; key `results:<tenant>:spam_complaints:<type>:dont`, retired like the others. `LearnedView.week` (`LearnedWeek`: `summary`, `dos`, `donts`, `retired`) from `weeklyLearningFor`, read with the member's own client beside the rules; null when unread (the rules still show). The switch defaults off, independently of the email-agent flag. Sample/fallback stores and the ordinary cron sweep remain code-only. The leased tenant supplies identity; memory/logs and runAi tenant reservations remain authoritative. Both Home and Plan allow 120 seconds; action budget is 100 seconds, provider calls 10 seconds, with 5 seconds reserved before another call. No live setting, credential or cap was changed.

- PSH-001 (2026-11-11): **the live Klaviyo draft push** (`features/klaviyo-push/`, behind lane A's `DraftPusher` port). It only ever makes or changes a DRAFT campaign: the Klaviyo client's `write` allows only the addresses that make or change a draft, its message's test settings, its variations, templates and pictures (`isDraftWrite`), and refuses any body carrying a status, send options or a send time (`carriesSchedule`); never a schedule, a send job, a campaign deletion, a list, a segment or a profile (D17). Writing drafts is **its own switch, the owner's: `KLAVIYO_DRAFT_PUSH=live`, off by default**, on top of KLV-001's `KLAVIYO_MODE=live`; the sample store's emails always get a sample draft. The build's content checks must have passed (`DraftInput.contentChecked`, QAG-001). The push follows Step 0's recipe that worked (docs/step0/README.md): the audience checked in the account, then pictures imported into Klaviyo's library (VISION rule 11), the final checks on exactly the HTML sent (pictures, the five footer tags, Gmail's 102KB; the content checks are the build's), one HTML template per design, the campaign with its audience and no message inline, then its message with design A. An A/B design test (EML-005, `DraftInput.variations`, exactly two, A first) is made in ONE message create with both designs and the even test (`winner_percentage` 0, no winner) and read back at once, so a draft never exists with two designs and Klaviyo's own A/B settings: a refused create makes nothing and the message is made with design A alone; a test not kept (then, or after a later change to the draft) has design B taken out at once; which variation is design A is saved from Klaviyo's answer to the create, else found by our names, else by what it shows (its template's HTML is ours), never by the order Klaviyo lists them (Klaviyo unwell while it looks: tried again; unknown while not yet safe: the even test set, then `ab_test_unsafe`; unknown on a safe draft: `designs_unknown`, which a later push looks at again, never a closed draft); an A/B draft not yet seen safe, even one whose create answer was lost, is checked first on the next run, before any other check and whatever the time, and Klaviyo being unwell then only makes the build wait (Klaviyo's own wait time is kept); a failure half way through changing a two-design draft makes it safe before the answer; a delete Klaviyo answers but does not show yet sets the even test meanwhile and waits, at most 10 minutes from its first answer (`delete_answered_at`), then `ab_test_unsafe`; an owner's change is looked for before design B is taken out, and the draft is then left. `DraftResult.designs` then says `'A'` (lane A alternates designs). Design B is never added to a draft afterwards (a draft made with one design stays one); if B cannot be taken out, the even test is tried as a last resort, else the push is refused (`ab_test_unsafe`). One push key, one draft: every step is saved in `klaviyo_draft_pushes` through `save_klaviyo_push(build, lease, step)`, worker only and under the build's exact push lease (`DraftInput.lease`), and what a push made stays made (its campaign, message, audience, first create time, design A after a refusal). A campaign create whose answer was lost is found again by its time and our mark (`GROS draft <key>`) matched in code, our name with no mark counting as ambiguous (another push's mark is that push's); a message whose answer was lost is taken over; a template by its exact name; a message or campaign create is never sent again before it could show (2 minutes). A template is marked deleted before its delete is sent, so it is never used again; ours is deleted once Klaviyo's copy is checked to hold our HTML, and one no variation uses (design B after the fallback, an older design) is deleted too. Subjects and previews are compared as Klaviyo may keep them (trimmed, one space in a row). The same key again updates the draft; one the owner scheduled, sent, deleted or changed in Klaviyo (a variation's subject or preview, its design, the A/B test, its mark) is never touched (`rejected`: `not_draft`, `externally_modified`). **The supervisor's answers (15 Nov):** a design edit is known per variation (`shown`: the template on it, Klaviyo's copy, and a fingerprint of that HTML as Klaviyo keeps it, so a copy not byte for byte ours is no false alarm; recorded as soon as the message is made or taken over, again right after each change Klaviyo shows (a read still showing the old template waits), and for every variation before a push is done: one without the time or an answer for it stops and the next run takes it), and every later push looks first: other HTML in that template, or another template on it, leaves the draft (`externally_modified`). A variation is marked only while a change of ours is on its way (another template on it is then ours) and unmarked when that change was not sent or was refused; lane A renders the Klaviyo-mode HTML and runs the content checks (QA split: the pusher checks only pictures, footer tags and size); a real email planned for a sample audience is refused before any Klaviyo call (`audience`); the session env forces `KLAVIYO_MODE=fake` and `KLAVIYO_DRAFT_PUSH=off`. A push never starts a Klaviyo request (6 s each) that might not end in its time (30 s; in the cron 25 s from the email step's start, whatever the inbox and plan steps took, and none past 45 s into the route; the cron leaves its scheduled jobs for the next run past 50 s; a run the platform stops is a lost answer, already handled): it answers `rate_limited` (30 s) and the next run goes on. Not live: the first real Klaviyo call waits for Raman's OK.
- LRN-001 (2026-11-12): **the Klaviyo results sync** (AGENT_MAP §5, D22; VISION §10 Sync with Klaviyo). One row per drafted email build (`klaviyo_email_results`: a live PSH-001 draft with its message, or a synthetic brand's sample draft, drafted in the last 30 days; a real brand's sample draft is in no Klaviyo account and is never followed) keeps what was planned and built (email type, angle, products, offer, audience, send time, subject, code, designs) for LRN-002. **Every hour** the results run (`/api/internal/klaviyo/results`, its own workflow at :44, off until `SCHEDULED_JOBS_ENABLED`, a peek first) claims due checks (`claim_klaviyo_results`: it first meets the drafts made since, then leases up to 40 for 3 minutes; claimed again while full batches come and time is left, at most 5 times) and reads each email's message in Klaviyo (`readDraft`, now with its send time, per-variation send times, send strategy and tracking parameters): draft, scheduled or sending (looked at again in an hour), sent, cancelled (also "Cancelled: …") or deleted (404: the end, also after its reads), or **changed outside the app** (its variations no longer match the subject and preview fingerprints PSH-001 last wrote; sticky, never overwritten: the pusher already refuses such a draft). A draft or a scheduled email two weeks past its day is stale (the end), unless the owner scheduled it later. A sent email's send time is Klaviyo's (or the earliest of its per-variation times), never ahead of now nor before the email was built, else when first seen sent (`context.sentAtFrom` says which). **After the send, results are read once a day for three days** (`save_klaviyo_result`: a day after the send and a day after the last read, three in all, each with what was read and how): one campaign report question per account for every due campaign (`readCampaignResults`: `/api/campaign-values-reports` by campaign, message, variation and its name, rows matched on the campaign because Klaviyo may give its own id as the message's; conversions on the store's Placed Order metric, else Clicked Email with no orders) and one Clicked Email count per email (`readLinkClicks`: `/api/metric-aggregates` by `$variation`, `URL` and `Bot Click`, by the message id, else, when people clicked and none came, by the campaign id; bots' clicks left out and counted; one question at least 350 ms after the last). Each address is mapped to its section (`emailSections`/`sectionOf`: BLK-001's `data-block` rows, the account's own tracking parameters left out; the clicker's `_kx`/`_ke` never kept) and each variation and click named as our design A or B. Each read keeps how it was made (`context`: its windows, the account's currency, the conversion metric, whether Klaviyo's 5-day attribution window was still open, the send strategy, whether an A/B draft's designs were read apart, how clicks were keyed, bots left out, whether the campaign was reported); a read is not `complete` when Klaviyo had more, gave no orders, did not split the designs, or a part could not be read. A campaign Klaviyo has not reported is waited for 12 hours, then its read is saved as not whole. Klaviyo is read only with the owner's `KLAVIYO_MODE=live` and a workspace still connected live, with its stored key, every request capped at 6 s, none started past 35 s and four requests' time kept for the results questions; **reads only** (GETs and the two report questions; the client posts only to report addresses). A rate limit pauses that account's checks for as long as Klaviyo says (at most a week); a refused key or a missing scope pauses them for 6 hours, an outage for an hour, logged without the key (D16); an answer we cannot read pauses only that email (or, for the report, the due ones). What a status read already said is kept when a check is put back. A check there is no point in is ended: a draft long past its day (stale; a scheduled one only after 45 days, as the owner may have moved it), a sent email unread for ten days since it was sent or met (final, saying why). A part of a read Klaviyo could not give keeps the earlier one (`context.resultsKept`/`clicksKept`); clicks that differ only by the clicker's token are one row. Time is kept back for the results questions (two requests' worth) only once an email is due; when the status reads run out of time, the due reads go on and the other statuses wait for the next run; when the results run out of time, what each status read said is saved. One check that cannot be saved is logged and left for the next run; it never stops the others. A synthetic brand's sample draft is a draft until its planned send time, then sent, with sample results growing over its three days. Shared edits: the Klaviyo client's report addresses gain `/api/metric-aggregates`; `findStoreMetrics` returns Klaviyo's own `clickedEmail`; `readDraft` returns `sendTime`, `firstSendTime`, `sendStrategy`, `trackingParams`; `reportRows` (ONB-103) is exported; PSH-001's fingerprints move to `features/klaviyo-push/fingerprints.ts`; the fake draft account can show a send time.

- APR-002 part 1 (2026-11-07): approval links (`features/approval/links.ts`, server only) are HMAC-SHA256 signed claims holding ids only: `v`, `tenant`, `sub` (the owner the email goes to), `batch`, `act` (`approve_all` with the shown emails, or `change` with exactly one), `items` as `[campaignId, revision]` pairs, a link id `jti` and an expiry 7 days out; one strict zod schema checks them on both sign and verify, and only the canonical signature spelling is accepted. Secrets are 32+ characters; the first signs, any in the list verifies (rotation). Who may use a link: holding it is the recipient owner's authority, but only while it still holds; at the button the server re-checks from membership, never from the claim, that `sub` is still an active owner of `tenant`, and a signed-in user must be `sub` (`other_user` otherwise). When a link is used up: opening it (GET) only calls `verifyApprovalLink` and shows a confirmation page, so mail scanners never approve or use it up; the button (POST) calls `redeemApprovalLink`, whose `ApprovalLinkStore.redeem` is one database command that locks the workspace, re-checks the owner, records `jti` once (unique key) and applies the action to exactly `items` in the same transaction, answering `used`, `not_owner` or `changed` (PT409 when a revision moved); nothing is recorded unless the action applies. Approve all from the email approves only the emails the email showed, at their revisions (APR-001 `approveAll(items, shown, …)`). `weeklyApprovalEmail` (`email.ts`) lists only emails still open (waiting and at least an hour ahead) soonest first, with date in the store timezone, offer, audience, phone screenshot and warnings; it signs the Approve all link for exactly the shown emails and each Change link once, refuses to build when nothing is waiting, escapes every word, keeps the subject on one line, accepts only clean https links, has a preheader, says when the links stop working, and does not invite replies until replies are read.

- APR-001 part 1 (2026-11-07): the weekly approval rules (`features/approval/weekly.ts`). A batch item carries its copy/design `revision`, send time, subject, offer, segment, state (`pending_approval`, `change_requested`, `needs_human`, `approved`), change rounds and whether the owner asked for a change. Every approval is bound to what the owner saw: `approveAll(items, shown, context, tenantId, now)` approves only the `{ campaignId, revision }` pairs shown, still waiting and at least `minimumLeadMinutes` (60) before the send, and reports every other email with a `SkipReason` (`skipWords` has the owner's words, with no product name); the store re-checks the revisions in the same transaction and raises PT409 when one moved. `requestChange(item, shownRevision, …)` sends a change to the AI at most twice (`maxChangeRounds`), the third to a person (VISION rule 13); `backForApproval` brings a redo or a person's finished version back as a new revision. The owner check is the shared `can(context, 'approve', tenantId)` (owner of that workspace only), never a second rule. `approvedWithoutEdits` is the share VISION tracks from the first client.

- ASM-003 (2026-11-07): `assembleFromLayout(input, brand, run, mode, layout, feedback)` (`features/assembly/modes.ts`) builds the client's email from a competitor layout (`layoutSchema`: the labelled `sections`, top to bottom, and an optional `angle`, checked on arrival). The angle is untrusted: a labeller wrote it after reading the competitor's email, so it never appears in the client's email in any mode, and it reaches the writer only as `strategyNote` inside the JSON data, with a rule that it describes structure only and that no name, number, claim, offer or phrase may be used from it. Exact keeps the sequence with the client's own content and words from the brief (the angle is not sent); Rebrand keeps the sequence and the angle's structure; Adapt passes the angle to ASM-001's planner (`assembleEmail(…, { strategyNote })`). `layoutSequence(layout, allowed, products)` keeps the order, budgets products the way `fill` takes them (so a 3-column grid after a hero may become 2 columns), gives a missing section the nearest block the client can fill (a stand-in, with a plain reason) and returns every section it left out (`dropped`: unsure, not a block type, over the 12-block cap). The fixed-sequence request lists each block with its word limits, tells the writer what a stand-in must not write about (no founder story for a founder note, no reviews for a review strip), carries ASM-001's `writerRules`, and sends `offer: null` when the layout has no offer section; a live answer must have every block in order, else `invalid_output` with feedback. Without a live writer, steps and FAQ sections become text and the sample words come only from the campaign type, brand and catalog. A layout with fewer than 3 usable blocks, or only header, announcement and footer, is refused. It returns ASM-001's fail-closed result (`ready`, `rewrite` or `sample`, with the same engine checks through the shared `finish`; only `ready` may go on, `checkAssembled`) plus `mode`, `layout`, `dropped` and `notes` for the owner (sections left out, no offer section for the client's code, no room for the brief's product in the layout, no angle found). Because the writer cannot add a product block to a fixed layout, a focus product the layout has no room for is a note, not a problem.

- ASM-001 part 1 (2026-11-07): `assembleEmail(input, brand, run, { feedback?, strategyNote? })` (`features/assembly/assemble.ts`) turns a brief into checked blocks. `AssemblyInput` carries the brief, the cleaned catalog, the client's codes, `maxDiscountPercent`, `sendAt`, the store `timezone`, the `facts` sheet and confirmed material; `DiscountCode` (`expiresAt: string | null`) and `BrandFacts` have exactly copy QA's shapes (ASM-002, #323), and part 2 imports them from `features/copy-qa` once it merges; `assemblyInputSchema` checks stored input at the job boundary (ISO times with an offset, a known IANA timezone); an unknown timezone also stops `assembleEmail`. The AI writes words only: products, prices, pictures, links, the offer's percent, the code and its end date (the last minute, in the store's timezone) are placed by code, and founder notes, review strips and customer photos only ever carry the client's own words (the model writes nothing for them). `allowedBlockTypes` offers a block only when material that fits it exists (`usableMaterial`): grids need enough products (at most 12 are used, `maxProducts`), `offer_banner` a listed code within the max that still works at `sendAt`, `review_strip` confirmed reviews that pass the block and a verified review source (`facts.reviewsVerified`), `founder_note` the founder's own note, `faq` a known fact, and buttons, banners and the photo hero a link (the store or a product). A product shows its old price only when the cleaning step marked it a temporary sale (`compareAtIsSale`) and the implied discount is within the max (Step 0 finding 2). Products never repeat. A focus product that cannot be placed stops the build (`AssemblyError` `focus_unavailable`, for a person). The writer gets the allowed blocks with their word limits, shared `writerRules` (no price, code or link; only the offer's own percent; shipping, delivery, returns and guarantees only from the facts; no results, social proof, founder story or false urgency), and the store's data as one JSON line marked as untrusted, with the last failed checks inside it; thinking is set to low with 4,000 output tokens. `assembleEmail` fails closed: it returns `Assembled`, either `{ status: 'ready', draft }`, `{ status: 'rewrite', draft, problems }` or `{ status: 'sample', draft }`, and only `ready` may go on; `checkAssembled(result)` is the one check part 2 merges with copy QA's in `withCopyQa`, and it never passes a rewrite or a sample. A result is `rewrite` when the engine finds anything wrong with what the email will print (the clipped words of the kept blocks, normalised with NFKC and without invisible characters): blocks not allowed, words over a limit, too few products left, the brief's product not shown, a product named that the email does not show, a percent (written `%`, `percent` or `per cent`) other than the placed offer's, or any percent without an offer block, shipping, delivery, returns or guarantee words that are not a fact line word for word (whether or not the fact is known), results or timings, social proof, a founder story, banned phrases. Only the titles of the products shown, the approved claims and the fact lines are masked first; questions are not read as claims. The order is put right without a retry: at most one announcement bar first, then the header, then the content (one offer, cut to the 12-block cap, never the header), then one footer; an answer with nothing usable is `AiRunError('invalid_output')` with feedback; provider failures keep their wait and diagnostic. With the AI port's fake the sample writer builds the email from the campaign type, brand name and catalog titles only (never the brief), never has problems, and says `source: 'sample'`; part 2 never sends a sample draft for approval. The draft lists the placed `productIds` and the `code`. `copyDraftOf(draft)` gives `checkCopy` the subject, preview and each block's words with prices, old prices and the code line.

- STAB-004 (2026-11-06): CI is split into three workflows. `ci.yml` (`verify`: format, lint, typecheck, unit tests, build) runs on every pull request and push to `main` and is the only check to require on `main`. `database.yml` (pgTAP) and `browser.yml` (Playwright plus the first-draft and email concurrency scripts) run on pull requests only when their files change, skip drafts, can be run by hand, and no longer re-run on push to `main`; both start a lean local Supabase (`-x studio,logflare,vector,imgproxy,edge-runtime,realtime,postgres-meta,supavisor`).
