- REF-003: implemented by Claude Code on the user's sequential request; root delegated these shared integration changes. (1) `postal-mime@4.1.4` pinned exact (zero runtime dependencies, explicit nesting/header/part/forward limits). Mailparser's own documentation marks it maintenance-only and recommends PostalMime; the only published PostalMime advisory (GHSA-f2hq-32vh-53cc) is fixed from 4.0.8. Declared charsets the runtime cannot decode are refused rather than read as windows-1252; `.html`/`.txt` must be UTF-8, BOM-marked or (HTML) `<meta charset>`-declared. (2) Durable pre-upload admission: `admit_email_file_upload` binds actor + tenant + request key + SHA-256 + kind + size + name and reserves capacity under the tenant lock (20/hour, 200 active, 500 added emails, 100 MiB stored-or-reserved distinct bytes) before any service-role write; `finalize_email_file_upload` enqueues one `email.import` job only after the stored object size is confirmed; replays resume at the interrupted step; nothing deletes objects, so an object used by another receipt is never removed. Storage allows overlapping writers to the same path (last wins) but refuses later ones; the path is the SHA-256 of the server-validated bytes and the worker re-verifies, so racing writers store identical bytes. (3) Trusted worker RPCs `claim_/finish_/fail_email_file_import` are service-role only, re-check active tenant and active uploader, and accept parsed output only for the frozen hash and still-stored object. Legacy `claim_job` (selection and stale sweep) and `private.onboarding_lease` (so `fail_job` and fixture finishers) now refuse `email.import` as well as `email.rewrite`; `job_runs_kind_check` gains `email.import`. (4) Trusted format: `reference_imports` gains `source_kind`, `file_import_id`, `content_format`; `create_email_result` is redefined in 90015 to use `content_format` when present (pastes keep the 90014 regex inference), and choose/preview/copy text version/rewrite worker read the same stored format (`sourceFormat`, `email_sources.format`). `pastedReadable` takes an optional trusted format. (5) New private bucket `email-imports` (5 MiB, html/plain/rfc822), no client write policy, owner/admin read policy for referenced objects. `GET /api/v1/email-imports/:id/file` and export `part=file` serve exact bytes; `part=original` keeps its meaning (decoded source). `next.config.ts` applies the sandbox CSP override to both download paths. (6) Server-only pilot gate `EMAIL_IMPORT_TENANT_IDS` (exact UUIDs, max 50, no wildcard) for any non-loopback or production Storage; checked before admission, before the write, on retry and on each worker attempt; independent of the unchanged OpenAI pilot gate. Root must add the blank name to `.env.example` (this session cannot read it). (7) `SubmitButton` gains optional `pendingLabel`/`disabled`; the setup reference step adds a secondary "Upload a file" link beside "Paste an email". (8) Review fixes: metadata/name/download shortening is surrogate-safe (`clipText`, `wellFormed`); HTML decoding follows BOM → explicit `<meta charset>` → UTF-8 and refuses undecodable declarations; dates outside years 1–9999 are dropped as metadata. (9) Narrow shared UI integration requested by root now that real rewriting is being configured: `AppShell` takes an optional `status` (default "Your workspace" / "Emails are saved privately"; admin and designer layouts pass their own truthful line) and shows the brand's demo copy only when `AUTH_MODE=demo`; the mobile menu shows the same status; the client overview footer reads "Sending and performance data use samples. Emails you add and create are saved." outside demo mode. `BrandPresentation` is unchanged, and no simulated sending/results behaviour changed. (10) Final deployment-compatibility correction: Vercel Functions cap request and response bodies at 4.5 MB (https://vercel.com/docs/functions/limitations, https://vercel.com/docs/errors/function_payload_too_large), so the raw upload/storage bound is 4 MiB (4,194,304 bytes) everywhere — browser hint and help text, action, parser, SQL `byte_size` and admission checks, bucket `file_size_limit` — keeping uploads plus multipart overhead and original-file downloads under the cap. Earlier REF-003 evidence used 5 MiB; it was superseded by this change and re-verified. The 100 MiB workspace cap, admission, pilot gate, 100,000-character decoded bound and the existing `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` (used by other upload features) are unchanged; files above 4 MiB need direct-to-Storage signed uploads, recorded as remaining. (11) Root supervisor integration, not overwritten by this task: blank `EMAIL_IMPORT_TENANT_IDS=` in `.env.example`; CI browser job runs `node scripts/test-email-import-concurrency.mjs` with a 25-minute browser timeout; the deployment snapshot was moved outside the repository. A narrow, supervisor-authorized test fix in `tests/e2e/email-generation.spec.ts` makes the preview-fit helper wait (retried poll, no sleep) until the published `data-scale` matches the measured container before the unchanged fit assertions.

- AI-002/REP-001: implemented by Claude Code on the user's explicit request for real OpenAI rewriting and exact source-email replication. This narrowly supersedes the historical "fake AI / structural reuse only" defaults for the pasted-email flow only: (1) a server-only OpenAI Responses adapter (native `fetch`, no SDK) behind the typed `AiProvider` port; `lib/providers/contracts.ts` gains optional `schema`/`reasoningEffort`/`timeoutMs`/`safetyIdentifier` request fields, optional response identity/cache fields and a typed `AiProviderError` (kind + billing `none|usage|unknown`). Default model `gpt-6.1-terra`, priced from the official pricing page; only priced models are accepted. (2) Exact copies: `email_sources` is a separate immutable, byte-exact copy of the owner's paste (update-blocking trigger); copy and rewrite results are immutable versions in `email_result_revisions`, synced as unapproved `campaign_content` revisions, so existing owner approval/design/delivery gates are unchanged and edits invalidate approval as before. (3) Paid work: `claim_/begin_/finish_/fail_email_generation` execute only as `service_role` (server worker), never for signed-in users; they re-check active tenant, active owner requester and frozen brand/source/target revision. Reservations bound the full serialized request (UTF-8 bytes + 2,000 tokens) plus full output; actual cost above a reservation is still recorded. Unknown outcomes are charged at the reservation and never retried automatically. (4) Shared legacy helpers are narrowed for the new kind only: `claim_job` (selection and expired-lease sweep), `private.onboarding_lease` (so `fail_job`/fixture completions refuse it), `reserve_/reconcile_fixture_usage` (refuse the `email-rewrite:` namespace and rewrite reservations); `private.reserve_budget` keeps identical accounting with truthful messages for rewrite spend. `job_runs` gains kind `email.rewrite`; `ai_calls.provider` allows `openai`/`sample`. (5) `parse5@8.0.1` is pinned as a direct dependency (already in the lockfile via jsdom) because sanitizing and editing untrusted email HTML needs a WHATWG parser rather than regex rewriting. (6) The import page now continues to `/create-email/<id>` (rewrite or copy); the outline composer remains one link away. (7) `next.config.ts` adds a later header rule giving `/api/v1/emails/:id/export` a `sandbox; default-src 'none'` CSP, because the app-wide CSP otherwise overrides route headers. (8) Browser tests start a loopback OpenAI test double (`scripts/fake-openai.mjs`); the app accepts plain-HTTP OpenAI base URLs only on loopback outside production. (9) Temporary production pilot gate: because every new workspace receives the synthetic starter package and workspace creation is uncapped, real OpenAI requests are default-deny and allowed only for exact workspace UUIDs in the server-only `EMAIL_REWRITE_TENANT_IDS` (max 50, no wildcard). It is checked on the choose/retry screens and on every worker attempt before reservation or dispatch; not-enabled queued jobs fail as `setup_required` (diagnostic `workspace_not_enabled`). Only the loopback test double outside production bypasses it. This is not a commercial entitlement or billing system; no SQL change.

- REF-002: implemented by Claude Code on the user's sequential request. Owner-pasted reference emails are a separate tenant-private source class (`origin = owner_import`), never competitor evidence or a synthetic watched brand. The original paste is stored exactly as received (CRLF included, up to 100,000 characters) and is immutable to clients; only a server-derived plain-text preview (line endings normalized, bounded at 20,000 UTF-16 code units with an explicit "preview limited" notice; if an astral character straddles the cutoff, only its high half is replaced by a one-unit ellipsis so no lone surrogate reaches JSON/Postgres) is ever displayed, always as React text, never as markup, iframe content or links. Source URLs are http/https without credentials, kept as a note and never fetched. The reusable outline is derived in SQL from paragraph breaks; caller-supplied structure or HTML is rejected. One guarded owner RPC with actor/tenant/payload-bound receipts makes retries idempotent; 500 imports per workspace. `create_first_draft` gains an `imported_reference` source that requires the exact tenant and records provenance (`analysis: none`, copy not reusable) without approval changes. Recent-choice lists are bounded: 12 in the composer (plus a preselected item), 5 on the import page, the latest 1 in setup. Rendering keeps its existing structure choices; an imported outline is not a rendering source. The integration owner narrowly assigned two existing browser specs to this task for test-only synchronization fixes (statistics worker-batch drain; planning approval completion predicate).

- DRF-001: continue sequentially from the user’s feature register. Build a dedicated composer using existing original/authorized structural campaign commands, without claiming generated creative is finished. Add actor/tenant-bound request idempotency behind one wrapper RPC and an unexposed private table. `ActionForm.preserveValues` opts the composer out of React’s automatic form reset so failed commands retain controlled selections. Local-date conversion uses the server-authorized tenant timezone, rejects nonexistent DST times and requires explicit ambiguity resolution. Preserve approvals/provider gates. Import only clean-room requirement descriptions into the repository register, never legacy code, prompts or runtime content. This branch is stacked on the still-open onboarding PR #2; do not merge or deploy it automatically.

- ONB-001: the user requested immediate implementation with onboarding as the priority. Add a resumable, server-derived first-use guide and reduce visible navigation. Preserve existing authorization, revision checks and fixture boundaries. Workspace creation redirects to `/get-started`; existing users keep their dashboard. Shared auth/navigation presentation and brand action cache invalidation are integration-owned changes in this slice.

- UI-002: the user requested a whole-product review and visual polish. Retain the neutral Inter/graphite/blue identity; improve the shared shell, owner overview and calendar, and fix narrowly evidenced usability defects. Cross-domain presentation and query edits are justified by this integration review: stable scoped collection reads, direct authorized detail reads, and current-tenant active-subscription choices for library/rendering/GROS. Existing action payloads, domain authority, exact approvals, provider gates and migrations remain unchanged. Reuse the existing checkout and preserve the pre-existing local preview/Supabase data. Use a disposable stack for mutating acceptance and record gaps separately from implemented fixture functionality.

- V2-011: domain mutations and worker leases lock the tenant before campaign/job/usage resources; expired reservations are released only without a live lease. GROS rechecks creator visibility after waiting for tenant/conversation locks and uses conversation-locked ordinals and bounded cursor pages; proposals require actual scheduling/assignment readiness before reservation. Plans freeze exact local custom events and canonical pinned-rule versions and reject changed inputs. Operator-only design escalation/resolution persists in campaign audit events with exact current workflow version and verified overdue SLA, without creative approval changes. Cron dispatch requires a secret, validated scope and explicit loopback fake mode; live webhooks return unavailable without ingesting content. Business stale-version/lease conflicts use `PT409` (HTTP 409), preserving checks and ACLs; custom `40001` caused infinite PostgREST 14 retries in the actual concurrent RPC check. Historical migration files stay intact, with the conversion in integration migration `20260914090011`. Source: [Supabase troubleshooting](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/troubleshooting/high-cpu-and-infinite-transaction-retries-when-using-custom-error-codes-in-rpc-functions-77326b).

- V2-010: every fixture sweep requires exact owner preview approval. Twelve calendar months (UTC) of purchaser protection wins over the 180-day order candidate rule; consent, bounce/spam, existing suppression and changed evidence are rechecked at each stage. Two original local winback audits precede ten-day nonresponse suppression. Concurrent active sweeps are rejected. Reversal removes only the optimizer reason when all consent/protected-reason checks pass. Dated fictional band pricing is an estimate with no measured savings. Own/reference reuse copies structural metadata into an unapproved original draft; cross-client publication remains off.

- V2-009: provider result contracts include explicit window bounds, completeness/comparability, currency and confounders. Send metadata freezes with the immutable package before provider creation. Learning uses complete seven-day same-cohort sends within thirty days, five per subject-length side; only owner-pinned preferences influence matching fixture copy and retain evidence lineage. Re-synthesis never changes dismissal. Ten consecutive first-time confirmed synthetic sends is the default L2 streak; any owner rejection resets its generation. L2 simulation is actor/policy/brand/version-bound at 72 hours; production L2 and design delegation remain constrained off.

- V2-008: GROS visibility is checked by RLS and every mutation; a shared conversation never transfers proposal authority. Package cycles retain immutable definitions, atomic synthetic usage is reserved before generation, and actual fixture usage is reconciled by operation. Verified-email invitation acceptance is derived from local Auth. Operator diagnostics contain metadata/counts only. The shared worker helper now treats a missing JWT role as denied, avoiding nullable-boolean authorization.

- V2-007: immutable provider schedule precision is milliseconds, matching the package ISO snapshot. L1 is an explicit revisioned owner policy; it does not grant general chat authority. Every provider mutation requires server-recorded conclusive reconciliation, not just a worker convention. Rescheduling retains provider identity while adding a new immutable package; rejected cancellation retains actual remote state. Only an explicit labelled simulated send creates a private own skeleton. Sent snapshots remain immutable during later asset/kit corrections. The live Klaviyo class remains disabled: public campaign/send-job contracts were checked, but hosted artifact, account acceptance and transport reconciliation are unverified.

- V2-006: deterministic fixture design artifacts use trusted, self-contained SVG strips in a private server-write-only bucket; text-email HTML remains readable without slicing. This needs no rendering dependency. SVG email-provider/client compatibility and aesthetic quality are externally unverified; live delivery stays disabled. Package assembly is rebuilt from approved sources, never caller HTML. Per-strip revisions retain unchanged content-addressed artifacts, and own templates remain tenant private and originate only from confirmed simulated sends.

| Decision            | Value                                                                                          | Reason                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Runtime             | Next.js App Router + TypeScript                                                                | One deployable web application with server-rendered role surfaces.                                         |
| Architecture        | Modular monolith with explicit domain modules                                                  | Fast MVP iteration without premature distributed-system overhead.                                          |
| Hosting             | Vercel                                                                                         | Preview deployments and server functions.                                                                  |
| Backend             | Supabase Postgres/Auth/Storage/Realtime/Queues                                                 | Durable relational core and tenant security.                                                               |
| Isolation           | Server authorization plus PostgreSQL RLS                                                       | Deny-by-default tenant boundaries with defense in depth.                                                   |
| Data access         | `@supabase/ssr` plus generated database types and SQL/RPC                                      | Keeps RLS authoritative and avoids a competing schema source.                                              |
| Validation          | Zod                                                                                            | Shared environment, form, action, and adapter validation.                                                  |
| UI                  | Tailwind CSS + accessible headless primitives                                                  | Fast, consistent, responsive implementation.                                                               |
| Tests               | Vitest + Playwright + pgTAP/SQL security tests                                                 | Covers code, user journeys, and RLS.                                                                       |
| Async               | Durable queue + idempotent workers                                                             | External API work must survive retries and timeouts.                                                       |
| Demo behavior       | Seeded fixtures + fake adapters                                                                | Complete workflow without external secrets or billable calls.                                              |
| Dates               | Store UTC; render in tenant IANA timezone                                                      | Removes the timezone contradiction found in the reference product.                                         |
| Money               | Integer micro-USD internally                                                                   | Avoids floating-point cost errors.                                                                         |
| IDs                 | UUID primary keys; external IDs in unique scoped columns                                       | Stable internal identity and provider reconciliation.                                                      |
| Visual system       | Cool neutral field, white panels, graphite actions, blue interaction cues                      | Matches the user-selected reference theme through original semantic tokens.                                |
| Design review       | Brand owner reviews/revises and approves the exact current design version                      | User-confirmed correction; admins handle assignment, SLA, and escalation.                                  |
| v2 build scope      | New implementation on existing foundation; email-first fake/fixture execution                  | Autonomous plan in `docs/OVERNIGHT_BUILD_PLAN.md`; external actions remain separately authorization-gated. |
| Approval / delivery | Revision-bound approvals; immutable package; reconcile unknown provider outcomes               | Aligns diagrams and target contracts; V2-000 owns code/type/migration integration.                         |
| Autopilot default   | L0 owner confirms; L1 standing policy after owner approvals; production L2/delegation disabled | Preserves owner design control while permitting simulated background scheduling.                           |

Confirmed: reference-neutral visual direction, white-label-first architecture, code-first build path, DRY shared implementation. The selected Impeccable direction uses seed `6f728f1c`; its durable contract is `DESIGN.md` plus `.impeccable/design.json`.

- SHP-001 / V2-D2 (2026-11-07): v2 is Klaviyo only (BUILD_BRIEF D2, VISION rule 1). Connections shows the Klaviyo card only; the Shopify card, form and `connectShopify` action are gone (the credential helpers, verifier, `shopify-read` port, `store-data` reader, `features/store` dashboard and the tables stay, unused, with no destructive migration). `/store` redirects to `/brand` and the Brand & Store tab row is not shown (one tab left). The Dashboard's UTM tile no longer asks to connect Shopify. Empty product lists say products will come from the Klaviyo catalog (the live catalog is V2-S3a, #310). The Sample data tools keep the product fixture, which still uses the internal `shopify` connection row for its `commerce.sync` job, but call it "sample catalog" on screen. The brand-mismatch guard keeps its Shopify checks; they never fire without a Shopify connection.

- RET-002 (2026-11-11): decisions D16 and D17. No weekly approval: `/copy-review` (the old weekly copy batch) answers 404 through the proxy like the RET-001 designer routes, and nothing links to it; APR-001/APR-002 code (`features/approval/`) stays unrouted and unscheduled. No human loop: `withCopyQa` answers `fallback` instead of `needs_human`; callers record one entry in `public.agent_fallbacks` through `public.record_fallback` (service role only; one row per tenant and dedupe key, a repeat counts `occurrences` and keeps the latest reason) using `copyCheckFallback` / `assemblyFallback` (`features/fallback/entry.ts`) and a `FallbackLog` (`features/fallback/log.ts`: database and memory versions; writing never throws). Platform admins read it on Admin → Operations through `public.admin_fallback_log(max_rows)`. Agents use short keys (`copy_check`, `assembly`, later `brand_inspector`, `section_tagger` …), so new agents need no migration. Lane B's `ops_tasks` (inbox) are unchanged.

- STR-001 (2026-11-11): the Brand pulse (`features/strategy/pulse.ts`). Code builds the evidence (each fact with an id and its words) and decides what may be offered: only real codes, valid on the window's first day, at or under the max discount (others are listed as left out with the reason). The agent (`brand-pulse`, purpose `review` = Flash, as AGENT_MAP's model table says; the Brief writer and Calendar planner will use `plan`) only picks evidence ids and says why, without numbers, codes or dates; `checkPulseAnswer` enforces that and out-of-stock products. Up to 3 tries with the exact problems; a refused call (cap, provider) is not retried; then `codePulse` and one fallback entry. The owner's pick is `OfferPick` (`auto`, `none`, `picked` offer ids from the pulse only); STR-003 stores it with the plan run. Sample store in `features/strategy/sample.ts` until lane B's readers land. After review: `readPulseInput` checks the store data (a bad brand or start throws; a bad row is left out and counted); `until` is the code's real last day, inclusive in store time (copy QA's `expiresAt` must be the end of that day); out-of-stock products are never launch or bestseller facts; `statedFact` (`features/strategy/words.ts`) refuses digits, money signs, number words, promise words ("free shipping"), weekdays, months and the store's codes as whole words; `tryAgent` (`features/strategy/retry.ts`) is the one retry loop for every agent.

- STR-002 (2026-11-11): the Competitor mapper (`features/strategy/competitors.ts`). Code keeps library emails of the same industry and size band from the last 90 days, places each on our 15 days (the same number of days, 0–7, before a date of the same kind: holiday, sale or event; or 0–6 days before month end when our month end is in the window), and groups them into patterns counted by distinct brands (at least 2). The agent (`competitor-mapper`, purpose `review`) sees only pattern ids, timing, types, offers, angles and counts (no email ids, brand ids, names or words), picks patterns and names each move without numbers or quotes; code writes "2 days before Public holiday: 3 of 5 similar brands. …" and the confidence (brand share). Same 3-try check and fallback as the pulse. `LibraryEmail` is the shape CI-001's Email classifier should feed. After review: its `industry`, `brandSize`, `emailType`, `offerType` and `angle` come from lane B's closed lists in `features/intelligence/taxonomy.ts` (CI-001, imported, not copied), so no competitor name, subject or phrase can ride in a label; untagged emails (null labels) are left out; rows that do not match (or have a broken date) are left out, and `readMapperInput` refuses a broken start.

- STR-003 part 1 (2026-11-11): `planFifteenDays` (`features/strategy/plan.ts`). Brief writer (`brief-writer`, `plan`) writes up to 8 actions (goal, fact ids from the pulse and the competitor moves, a date range in the 15 days, an allowed offer or none); Calendar planner (`calendar-planner`, `plan`) turns them into up to 10 slots (action, date, local time, one of 8 email types, angle, up to 3 products, offer, audience); the calendar rules (`calendarProblems`, code) refuse days outside the window or the action, no-email days, unknown or out-of-stock products, offers not allowed or already ended, unknown audiences, numbers in angles, more than the owner's sends per week, two emails to one audience on a day, and, with the shared planning policy, offers above 40% of a week's emails and offers closer than 7 days; the Strategy critic (`strategy-critic`, `review`) adds its own problems. Up to 2 rounds give the planner both lists; whatever still fails is dropped and logged. Agents that cannot answer fall back to `codeBrief` / `codeSlots` (logged); a critic that cannot answer leaves the rules alone (logged). Facts, prices and codes in the plan come from code, never from an agent. After review: `readPlanInput` refuses a pulse for other days, bad dates or send times, and keeps only the pulse's own offers; the kept plan is re-checked after every drop (`keepPassing`), so dropping an email can never leave a week above the offer share; the planner gets its previous plan with slot indexes and every problem when revising, the round with the fewest failing slots is kept, and a planner refused while revising keeps its best plan; the critic has the usual 3 tries; rules have stable keys (`CalendarRule`), new ones tie offers to offer emails, keep send times in 07:00–21:00 and refuse products before their launch day; `existing` covers the 7 days before the window too; drops are logged under `calendar-rules` (with the rule keys) or `strategy-critic`; the planner sees at most 30 products; with 2 emails a week no offer fits, and the plan says so in `notes`.

- EML-001 (2026-11-11): layer 1 of the email build (`features/email-build/sections.ts`). `BuildMode` is `copy` (D1 Exact: the competitor's tagged sections through ASM-003's `layoutSequence`, code only), `remix` (the competitor's angle as a structure-only `strategyNote`) or `scratch`. `Variant` (`id`, `family` = one of the 20 block types, `industries`, `emailTypes`, `score`) is the library shape CI-002's Variant maker should feed; until then `seedVariants` has one `<family>/seed` per type. `searchVariants` keeps allowed families for the industry and email type, best results first, 3 per family. The `section-planner` agent (purpose `copy`, Flash) picks variants by id; `checkSections` requires real variants of allowed families, the logo header first (after an optional announcement bar), the footer last, one button, one hero, products within the slot's count and an offer banner only with an offer. Then the usual 3 tries and a logged fallback to a safe layout per email type (`codeSectionPlan`), which always passes the check. `maxOutputTokens` is the answer's room only: MEM-002 (#370) adds the Gemini 2.5 thinking budget in the provider.
- EML-002 (2026-11-11): layer 2 of the email build (`features/email-build/content.ts`). Code locks each value from its source: products from the catalog (`productLock`: in the catalog, featurable, https photo, fits a product section, a known price; a repeated id counts once, the first), the slot's offer from the discount codes (`offerLock`: on the list, within the max, still working at send time; the percent and end come from the code, the end shown in store time), pictures from the catalog or the confirmed photos, links by `storeLink`'s rule. What cannot be locked becomes a safer choice: another product, no offer (also when no offer section is left, so the writer never gets a code it cannot show), a smaller product section (`product_grid_3col` → `product_grid_2col` → `product_feature`), a product hero for a picture hero without a photo, or no section; replaced sections use the family's seed variant and the email always keeps a message. At most 6 products are locked (`maxLocked`, the job boundary's `focusProductIds` limit). The `content-locker` agent (purpose `copy`, Flash, no thinking) only places product ids into the product sections, and only when there is a choice; `checkPlacement` enforces exact counts, known ids, each once, the plan's main product first and planned products before others; 3 tries, then plan order (logged). Changes are logged once per email as `content_replaced` with fixed words (`changeWords`, `didWords`) and the change keys. Contracts: `LockedContent.input` is the narrowed `AssemblyInput` (only the locked products in section order as `focusProductIds`, only the locked code as `offerCode`); `assembleLocked` (`features/assembly/modes.ts`) is the Copywriter on exactly the locked sections, so each locked product lands in its locked section (tested from the lock to the written email). Shared changes in ASM-001/003: `productTakes` is the one product-placement rule (`fill` and the sample writer): a grid shows 4 or 6 only when the later product sections still get their fewest (`minProducts`, also used by the Section planner); `layoutSequence` budgets the fewest products per section; `storeLink` uses a store link only when it is a real link, the first product's page only when there is none, and no link sections when it is broken.
- EML-003 (2026-11-11): the end of layer 2 (`features/email-build/inspect.ts`). `writeAndInspect` runs the Copywriter on the locked sections (`assembleLocked`), then code checks first, every round: assembly's own problems, copy QA (`checkCopy`, ASM-002) on the locked facts and code, a lock check (the draft shows exactly the locked products and code), `priceChecks` (a money amount the writer writes must be exactly a locked product's price) and `emailChecks` (subject at most 60 characters, at most one exclamation mark and no capitals words, preview 20 to 140 characters and not the subject, `spamPhrases`, no web or email address typed into the words, one button section, every link one the Content locker locked, alt text on every picture, at most 300 words). The checks read only the writer's words: `protectedText` masks product names, the brand name, the code, its percent and end, reviews, the founder's note and photo descriptions, so the writer is never asked to change what it cannot. Code is the final word: only a draft that passes code goes to the `brand-inspector` (purpose `review`, reads the Brand book and do's and don'ts) and the `email-inspector` (purpose `label`); each returns problems with a field, an exact quote of the writer's own words (`checkInspection` refuses store words), a reason and a fix; a draft seen before reuses its verdict. Feedback carries the last two rounds' reasons. The first write plus `rewriteRounds` (3) rewrites; then plain copy (`assembleLockedPlain`: facts-only words that never say "new", subject within 60, `Draft.source` `plain`), which must pass the same code checks, else nothing is built. Writer errors: busy or down (`rate_limited`, `unavailable`, `timeout`, `ledger_unavailable`) returns `retry` for the job; no writer (`cap_reached`, set-up or account problems, refusals) and the fake writer go to plain copy with their `cause` (`allowance_used`, `no_live_writer`; plain copy from the fake is sample-mode copy and must be treated like ASM-001's sample drafts); a wrong-shape answer is a round with its exact problems; `AssemblyError` and bugs throw. One fallback entry per email (`copy-inspectors`, `copy_plain_fallback` or `copy_failed`) with the cause and only code rule keys as candidate don'ts for LRN-002; an inspector that cannot answer is logged once and skipped. Contracts: `Draft.source` gains `plain` (ASM-001); `writerRules` gains the inbox limits.
- STR-003 part 2 (2026-11-11): "Plan next 15 days" end to end. Migration `strategy_runs` (number at merge, D24): one open run per workspace (`pulse_queued` → `offers_ready` → `plan_queued` → `planned`, or `failed`), starting tomorrow in the store's timezone; owner commands `start_strategy_run(t)` (returns the open run, or replaces one whose days have begun, closing it as `out_of_date`) and `pick_strategy_offers(t, run, pick)` (`auto`, `none`, or `picked` offer ids the pulse lists; PT409 when the run is not waiting or its days have begun); service-role job commands `claim_strategy_run(target)` (one run or the oldest waiting, active workspaces only, 5-minute lease, skip locked, a failed step waits a minute, a step out of 3 attempts is failed and the claim looks on), `finish_strategy_pulse`, `finish_strategy_plan` and `fail_strategy_step(run, lease, code, final)` (exact leases; `final` fails at once when a retry cannot help). Even the service role writes only through the commands. **Cron contract change:** the sweep (`/api/internal/jobs`) now runs plan steps for at most 5 s right after the inbox step, before the workspace jobs, and reports `plans: { ran }`. This is safe because `runStrategyRuns` (`features/strategy/worker.ts`) runs only the code-only path while store data is the sample store (no AI call, nothing metered, nothing logged as a fallback); the AI agents are wired into the job with the first real store reader, with their own time limit and a lease long enough for paid steps. The owner's click runs his own run right after the reply (`after()`). Saved pulses and plans are re-checked on read (`features/strategy/stored.ts`) by the screen and the job. Store data comes through the `StrategyData` port, which says when it is the sample store; the screen says so plainly. The `/plan` screen (sidebar: Plan next 15 days) starts a plan, shows progress, the pulse and the offer pick (ticked offers with "you choose" or "no offers" are refused, never dropped), then every planned email with its reason and facts; staff see it read-only; a plan whose days have begun offers "Start again".
- EML-004 part 1 (2026-11-11): layer 3 of the email build (`features/email-build/design.ts`). Approach A (`designA`) renders the draft's blocks with the BLK-001 renderer; approach B (`designB`) swaps the first `hero_product` picture for a designed one from `HeroImagePort` (made from the real product photo; `designedPictureOk`: plain https, no `data:`, no user or password). Each look takes desktop (600px) and 375px screenshots through `ScreenshotPort`; code checks first (`no_screenshot`, `broken_images`, `phone_overflow`), and only a clean look goes to the `visual-inspector` (purpose `review`, Brand book): for B it also gets the original product photo and the designed section's number, and must report any words, numbers, prices, codes or logos in the picture or a changed product (VISION rules 9 and 10). Before live use: a screenshot browser job like INB-002's, the Gemini 2.5 Flash Image adapter with its price in `lib/providers/gemini-pricing.ts`, and the owner's OK.
- EML-004 part 2 (2026-11-11): "Create email" end to end (D17). Migration `email_builds` (number at merge, D24): one build per planned email at a time (`build_queued` → `push_queued` → `drafted`, or `failed`) and one `push_key` per planned email: a new build after a failed one that reached the push keeps its key, so "Try again" never makes a second Klaviyo draft (blueprint: unknown remote outcomes reconcile before a repeat). The owner's `create_email_build(t, run, slot)` (owner only, tenant locked first, the latest plan only, the run planned, the email's day not passed in the workspace's timezone; clicking again returns the open or drafted build); service-role `claim_email_build` (pushes first, 5-minute lease; brings the planned email, the push key, the workspace timezone and the plan's first day; a failed step waits a minute; 3 attempts), `finish_email_build`, `finish_email_push`, `fail_email_step(code, final, retry_after_seconds)` (a busy Klaviyo's wait is kept in `not_before` and does not use up an attempt, at most 20 waits). `buildEmail` is the code-only path for now, like STR-003 part 2: the safe section layout, products placed in plan order by the Content locker (`agent: false`), plain facts-only copy that must pass every code check, coded design A; no AI call. It builds in the workspace's one brand timezone (`tenants.timezone`), reads offers through DSC-001's `OfferSource` at the send time (`offersAt`: no answer or no max means no discount), and the sample store starts from the plan's first day. Offers (supervisor, 11 Nov): `ownerOrSampleOffers` reads `SupabaseOfferSource.managed` with the job's service-role client; a saved max (a `brand_offers` row) or any active code wins, even while the store is the sample store; only when the owner saved nothing do the sample offers from the plan's first day apply; a failed read gives no discount, never the sample. Limits: after 5 failed builds a planned email is not built again (PT409); a step whose planned day has passed (store time) fails as `day_passed` when claimed; the push step gets its own attempts and waits; a built email needs a subject. A product is unfeaturable only when its stock is known to be 0 (`featurableStock`): unknown stock is allowed. `runEmailBuilds` checks the built email's shape and size before storing it, fails refused finishes at once, and pushes through `DraftPusher` with the push key; the owner's click runs both steps right after the reply, the cron sweep runs up to 10 waiting steps in 5 s. `DraftPusher` (`lib/providers/klaviyo-draft.ts`, contract agreed with the supervisor): draft only, never schedule or send; one idempotency key per planned email, and the same key updates that draft to the email just built (a draft the owner already scheduled or sent is refused as `rejected`, never changed); never throws, failures as `auth`, `rate_limited` with `retryAfterSeconds`, `unavailable`, `rejected` with the failing launch checks; it uploads the pictures and runs the launch check before creating the draft; a `sample` email is refused by a live adapter; PSH-001 builds it, `fakeDraftPusher` until then. `StoreSource` (`features/email-build/ports.ts`) is sample until lane B's readers. The plan shows each email's state ("Creating…", "Putting it into Klaviyo…", "Sample draft (not in Klaviyo)" or "In Klaviyo as a draft", or the failure's reason with "Try again"); no button for a day that has passed. `/plan/email/[buildId]` shows the built email through the safe preview (`previewHtml`, `ScaledFrame`) with plain notes.

- REL-FTR (2026-11-15): the email "Create email" stores (and the A-vs-B test's two designs) is drawn as Klaviyo gets it: the footer has Klaviyo's five tags (brand, address, unsubscribe, preferences, view in browser) and every picture must be an https link (`designA`, `designB` in `klaviyo` mode). Before, it was drawn in preview mode, with dead "#" footer links and no tags, so once release QA is wired (today the live pusher first refuses every build as `content_not_checked`) a live push would have refused every email as `footer_missing`. Our own screens and the screenshots for the visual check show the tags as placeholders (`previewFooterTags`); the renderer escapes every `{` and `}` in the words, so the footer's tags are the only ones replaced. An inline (`data:`) picture now stops the build at its design step as `render_failed` instead of at the push (store pictures, products and logos are https links; the A-vs-B test skips such an email as `render_failed`).

Its checks fit any model's emails, so a run on a live model can be scored the same way later (only with the owner's OK). Changing what the golden set expects needs a reason in the pull request.

- DST-004a (2026-11-15): **the Design critic** (D25, AGENT_MAP §4 layer 3 step 6, owner pick #8). The Design critic (`design-critic`, purpose `review`, Flash with the pictures) looks at one designed section as drawn (in Copy mode with its reference section, never reading the reference's words; with the original photo when given) and scores it 1 to 10 on a fixed checklist every time: hierarchy, spacing, contrast, alignment, the product or photo, and the phone (375 px). - PIC-26 part 1b (2026-11-16): **the subject line lab** (owner pick #26 "Subject line lab"; `features/email-build/subject-lab.ts`, on part 1a's evidence). Up to 10 subject ideas for one email (`labSize`) are weighed against how the store's own past emails were opened, and the best two are kept: A goes out, B is the one worth testing against it. An idea's score is the sum of its traits' lifts (`learnFrom`, part 1a); a trait the store's emails do not show counts only by a small rule of thumb (short +0.5 points, long -1, an exclamation mark -0.5), which a trait they show never gets. Ties keep the writer's order (its own pick first). The open rate it points to (`expected`) is the store's mean moved by each trait with evidence, by how much more or less the idea has it than the store's emails do (a trait half of them have moves it half its lift either way). Ideas the same but for case and spacing count once (the same subject again is tried while none of its spellings fitted, since another preview line may), at most 10 are tried; an empty one or one over 120 characters is left out; the caller's checks (`fits(subject, index)`: the copy checks, a subject another email of the plan has, the preview line written with it) leave out an idea before it is weighed, and each idea keeps its place in the list given (`index`, to find its preview line again). B is the best idea after A that differs from it in a trait (`tests` names them: what the test teaches), has less than 60% of the two ideas' words in common, and scores at most 5 points below A (`testMargin`, `worthTesting`: half the audience gets it); none: no test. `subjectLabVersion` is kept with what it picks. Each idea comes with up to three reasons in the owner's words, the strongest first ("Subjects that ask a question: 31% opened, the others 26% (6 of 12 emails)."; none when the two rates round the same) and, with evidence, the open rate the store's emails point to. Plain code, no AI and no database: the same ideas and history give the same pick.
- PIC-26 part 1a (2026-11-16): **what a subject does, and what the store's past emails say about it** (owner pick #26 "Subject line lab"; `features/email-build/subject-traits.ts`). Each subject has traits found by plain code (`traitsOf`): short (30 characters or fewer, a first-name tag read as a name, a logic tag and unseen characters left out), long (more than 50; a phone shows about 35), a question, a number (only in a subject without an offer), an offer (`offerWords`, ONB-103's), an emoji (a flag and a keycap too; never ©, ® or ™), the reader's first name (Klaviyo's tag, in its three spellings), the store's name (as a whole word, or its tag), a deadline as a phrase ("ends tonight", "ends in 3 hours", "24 hours only", "today only", "last chance"; never "the story never ends"), an exclamation mark, all lower case (never a script without capitals), something new (new, just in, back in stock, restocking; never "New Year", "New York" or "just in time") and "you" ("yourself" too); a tab or a line break is a space. The past emails that can teach (`pastSubjects`) are the history's sent emails with a subject of at most 300 characters, an open rate above 0 (none opened is opens not tracked) and at least 100 recipients, never an A/B test (its rate mixes two subjects) or one still collecting its results. With 10 of them or more (`minPastEmails`), each trait shown by at least 3 emails, and missed by at least 3 (`minPerSide`), gets the difference between the mean open rate with it and without it, shrunk by how sure it is (d² / (d² + se²), se the difference's noise from each group's own spread of open rates, never below the store's spread and at least 1 point, and how many emails each side has: one lucky email among three is noise, not a trait) and kept within 15 points (`learnFrom`); its two open rates and counts are kept for the reasons the lab gives in the owner's words (`traitWords`). Fewer emails, or a trait too few show, say nothing. Plain code, no AI and no database: the same history gives the same evidence.

A date counts for a window when its emails start inside it, so 1 to 15 December includes Christmas. `planningKeyDates(db, ...)` reads the saved country (or the timezone guess) and own dates, null on any failed read; `toPulseDates` gives the pulse's date rows (a sale is an event there). Review text is anyone's words, so a phrase is kept only when any email could say it as the brand: copy QA (`checkCopy`) and the writer's own word checks (`wordProblems`) pass it with the brand's real facts (no shipping, delivery, returns, guarantee or percent, no social proof, results, timings, founder story, banned phrase or general claim; a fact is said in the facts sheet's words, never a customer's), and it is not the customer or a family speaking (I, me, my, we, our), a superlative, ranking or comparison (best, only, better than, -est), an effect on the body (a body or skin word, soothes, calms, gone, game changer, after one wash), a rating (stars, 5/5; never one customer's rating, even when the brand's reviews are verified) or someone's name (a capitalised word other than the brand's and its products' names, a capitalised first word doing something, or thanks to someone). A fixed list of risky phrases per industry (the CI-001 industry list), in groups, each with a plain reason: broad green words (every brand); medicine claims for skincare, beauty, haircare and beauty tools (a skin condition only with a verb: "clears eczema", never "eczema-prone skin"); illness claims for supplements, wellness, fitness and food and drink; weight loss for supplements, wellness and food and drink, and only fast or certain weight-loss promises for fitness ("fat-burning moves" is exercise copy); germ killing; pests; pet health and vet endorsements (never "treats …", the product in pet copy); baby safety and pediatrician endorsements; drink health; toughness; jewelry sourcing. **The brand's industry in its own words** is read by the new `industriesInWords`/`industryInWords` (`features/onboarding/industry.ts`): whole words only, counted per industry, most words first, ties to who it is for (pet, baby) and then the more specific product (`industryOf` in the classifier matches parts of words and stays for an admin's short niche words). A known two-word name ("ice cream", "hair tools") counts twice and uses up both its words. The claims list takes the groups of every industry named with at least half the words of the top one ("Pet accessories" gets pet and accessories; one "home" in a clothes sentence brings nothing), and the general weight group only when supplements, wellness or food and drink is named more than fitness. Phrases are never one already on copy QA's general list. `withClaimsSafety(facts, industry)` adds them to the brand facts' `bannedPhrases`, which copy QA blocks: the brand's own banned words all kept, first, and the list fills what is left of the assembly input's 200; a phrase is not added when a claim the brand stands behind contains it in any spelling (space, hyphen or none: approving "carbon neutral shipping" also allows "carbon-neutral"). Copy QA's wording for such a block stays "on this brand's banned list"; `claimReason` gives the plain reason for the Brand book page.

- ONB-SITEb (2026-11-20): **a site read that finishes late never replaces a newer read's findings, loses nothing the newer read did not read, and a read of a website the brand no longer has never makes its findings current** (ONB-101's known issue, and the website change found in review). Site reads can finish out of order: a read asked for earlier may finish after a newer one (a retry, a slow page), and a read asked for again the same day keeps its row and so its first time (`start_site_reading` re-queues today's read). Until now `record_site_findings` kept all of a late read's findings already replaced as soon as any newer read had current findings, even for kinds of page the newer read never read, and whatever website that newer read was of. **The rules now, when a read finishes** (migration `20260914090093_site_findings_order.sql`): **R1** its website (the job's `input->>'domain'`, as the start functions write it) is not the brand's website now (`private.site_domain` of the saved `brand_profiles.domain`, read under the tenant lock that saving the brand takes first too; no website saved, or one that is no name such as an address, is never its website): all its findings are kept for the record, already replaced, and it replaces nothing; its job records whether its findings were made current (`checkpoint.current`). **R2** otherwise, for each kind of page it read: a newer read of the same website (asked for later, `created_at`; same workspace) that has finished, made its findings current and read that kind of page (its job's recorded `pages`, marked `read`, of a kind the reader reads) wins: the read's findings from that kind are kept already replaced, and it replaces nothing there; with no such read, its findings from it are current and replace the earlier ones of that kind, as if it had finished in order. A newer read that read a page and found nothing there still wins (as it does when it finishes last); one still queued or running, a failed one, one that recorded no page or whose job holds no pages, one kept only for the record by R1 (A, then B, then A: a newer read of A that finished while the website was B takes nothing), and another workspace's, take nothing; a read recorded before this rule (no `current`) counts as made current, as it was. **R3** it also replaces every current site finding of the workspace whose read was of another website (tenant-scoped, site findings only: the ads and reviews readers keep their own); a finding whose read names no domain is left as it is (none can exist today: every site read is started with its domain). **The same day back to a website** (`start_site_reading`, `create or replace` in the same migration, same signature, grants, tenant-first lock and errors): today's finished read of the saved website is queued again when a read of another website finished after it (`job_runs.updated_at`), as a failed one already was; otherwise once a day, as before. Without it, after A, then B, then A on one day every current site finding stayed B's (R3 had replaced A's) until the next day, and the Brand step would open on B's facts. **Why:** for the brand's website, the current findings are, for each kind of page, those of its newest finished read of that page that was made current, whatever order the reads finish in (the same reads in either order give the same findings, compared directly in the tests), and none of another website's once one of its own reads finishes. No tie-break on equal `created_at` (the older tests rely on ties being "not newer"). `record_site_findings` is `create or replace`d from its latest body (`090089`; no later migration redefines it), only these rules changed; `security definer set search_path = ''`, the grants (the worker only), the tenant-first locks (`private.onboarding_lease`, which refuses a lost lease with `PT409`) and RLS as before. **Known gaps, not fixed here:** `start_ads_reading` and `start_reviews_reading` re-queue only a failed read, so the same day back to a website keeps the other website's ads and reviews until the next day; the logos, photos and fonts keep "the newest read by `created_at` wins", so a re-queued read of the morning cannot replace the other website's logos, photos or fonts the same day; a read of the old website that is still waiting when the owner changes his website is still taken and paid for (its findings are then only kept for the record).

Faces for other scripts (Google's Cyrillic, Greek…) keep no file. A range is read as CSS reads it: Latin when its spans hold A, Z, a and z (`U+0041-005A, U+0061-007A` too), wildcards (`U+00??`) read, an invalid or empty range every character; one too long to keep whole keeps no file. It also lists at most 12 stylesheets to read later, **font services first** so the brand's own never crowd them out: Google Fonts `css` and `css2` links naming a family (`google`; their families are read whatever the cap), Adobe kits (`use.typekit.net/<kit>.css`, also from the older kit script; `adobe`), known font CDNs (`fonts.bunny.net`, `fast.fonts.net`, `cloud.typography.com`, `fonts.cdnfonts.com`; `cdn`), then the brand's own host, its subdomains and `cdn.shopify.com` (`site`; never a look-alike such as `cedarlane.com.evil.com`), from `<link rel="stylesheet">`, `rel="preload" as="style"` and `@import` (in the page or a sheet, read from that sheet's address; a sheet's last one needs no `;`). **What it reads:** inline `<style>` blocks (`@font-face` family, weight, style, `unicode-range` and `src`, also inside `@media`; rules whose selector's last part is a heading (`h1` to `h6`, `.h2`, `…heading`, `…headline`, `…title`; never inside `:not()` or `:has()`) or the body (`html`, `body`, `:root`), by `font-family` or the `font` shorthand, whose size may be a length, a keyword, `calc()`, `clamp()`, `min()`, `max()` or a `var()` before a line height), `style` attributes on `h1` to `h6`, `body` and `html`, and custom properties named for a family, followed through `var()` (4 steps, its fallback when undefined; custom properties keep their case). A custom property names a family only when its name has a font word and ends in family, stack, primary or typeface, perhaps then a role (`--font-heading-family`, `--typeHeaderPrimary`, `--font-stack-header`), or is `--font-<role>` (`--font-heading`); never `--font-display` (`swap`), `--font-heading-stretch` (`condensed`), `--font-rendering`, `--font-variant-caps` or the like. A family list counts by its first name only (the rest are fallbacks), so a system stack (`-apple-system, …, Roboto`) counts for nothing. **Names** are only those the design studio takes: its own rule, now exported (`fontFamily` in `features/studio/section.ts`); matched without case, spelled as the site's `@font-face` declares them. **Never:** keywords (`serif`, `system-ui`, `inherit`, and font values such as `swap`, `center`, `uppercase`), an unquoted name starting with a digit (`20px`, `2rem`), fonts on most devices (Arial, Helvetica, Georgia, Segoe UI…) unless the brand or Google serves them, icon fonts (Font Awesome, Material Icons and Symbols, icomoon, slick, glyphicons, ionicons, Judge.me's, a font named only `feather` or `star`…; "Lone Star" is a name), or a file that is `data:`, EOT, SVG or any other type (only one named `.woff2`, `.woff`, `.ttf` or `.otf`, or, like Adobe's, named for none with its `format()` given), not https, on a private or one-word host, with a port or a name and password, or over 1,000 characters. **An Adobe kit's link names no families** (they are in its stylesheet): a family used with no file found stays `unknown` until part b reads the kit. Part b fetches `stylesheets` and calls `siteFonts` again with them as `sheets` (`Sheet`: the address it was read from after redirects, which its files and imports are read from, and its text), with the same caps (this replaces a separate stylesheet reader). **Hostile input:** a value too long to read whole is refused or dropped, never cut and used (an address over 1,000 characters, in a link or an `@import`; the last declaration of a `style` attribute over 500 characters; the last selector of a list over 2,000); CSS is read once, left to right (comments, strings and brackets as CSS reads them; each selector read once, however many nested rules split its rule; nesting deeper than 64 counted, not read), at most 500,000 characters per block or sheet and 2 million in one call; at most 500 faces, font declarations, custom properties and links; the page is parsed once (2 MB) and walked without recursion; a page address that cannot be read, or any failure, gives an empty result. `publicHost` is now exported from `photos.ts` (unchanged).

- KLV-LOCK (2026-11-23): **the Klaviyo write lock** (contract change, `lib/providers/klaviyo/client.ts`, `lib/env/server.ts`; docs/KLAVIYO_WRITE_LOCK.md). Locked by default. While locked, the only requests that leave the app are an exact `GET` to `https://a.klaviyo.com` and an exact `POST` to one of three read-only report questions at exactly `https://a.klaviyo.com` + `/api/campaign-values-reports`, `/api/flow-values-reports` or `/api/metric-aggregates` (`reportQuestionPaths`: exact names, never a prefix or pattern; the three main already used, documented as read-only report queries in Klaviyo's API 2026-10-15). Everything else (PATCH, PUT, DELETE, any other POST, other methods or case, other origins or ports, `http`, a user in the address, a query, a trailing slash, case, percent-encoding, `.`, `..`, `//`) is refused as the new `KlaviyoError` kind **`write_locked`**, before any network call: in the client (`write()` first, then `send()` before the transport) and again in `fetchTransport` itself, from the method and address alone; `fetchTransport` also never sends to another origin, locked or not. `query()` keeps its own rule, now exact (no trailing slash): another address is `rejected`. The live pusher refuses a push up front while locked (its key is not read), as `rejected` (final, not retried). Released only by the server-only env **`KLAVIYO_WRITE_LOCK`** with exactly `unlocked`, read at each request (`klaviyoWritesUnlocked`, never cached; no option, argument, setting, RPC, screen or agent tool can release it); it wins over `KLAVIYO_MODE` and `KLAVIYO_DRAFT_PUSH`. **Only a separate, later, explicit owner instruction may unlock it; connecting a full-access key is not that instruction.** Tests that write to recorded accounts release it in their own blocks with `vi.stubEnv`, never globally.
- ONB-ORD (2026-11-20): **cancelled and refunded orders are left out of what the Catalog analyst and the Klaviyo historian count** (the known issue of ONB-102 and ONB-103). `findStoreMetrics` also finds the store's **Cancelled Order** (Shopify's spelling; **Canceled Order**, the spelling of Klaviyo's guide for stores without a built-in integration, too) and **Refunded Order** metrics, a store platform's own first as for Placed Order; a store without one has none of them (null: nothing is read, not an error). `readOrderReturns` (`lib/providers/klaviyo/catalog.ts`) reads their events of the window through the orders' own events address and page cap (`maxEventPages`, each page only while `more()` allows it); an event Klaviyo sends twice (the same id) is kept once (`readEvents`, for every reader). **These reads only correct the counts** (`correctionLeftOut`): any failure (an outage or a timeout, a 403, a refusal, an odd answer) leaves that read out; only a refused key or Klaviyo's pace stop the job, as before. Code matches each cancel and refund to an order read (`features/onboarding/catalog/returns.ts`, `matchReturns`) by the order's id: an integration's `OrderId` when the event has one (never then its `$event_id`), else `$event_id` (Shopify's order id, on its Placed, Cancelled and Refunded Order events). Amounts count whatever their sign (-25 and "-25.00" are 25). A cancel, refunds that come to the order's value, or a refund that says neither how much nor which lines (Shopify sends full refunds only) take the whole order out; a partial refund takes out its value and the units of the lines it lists, unless it only repeats the whole order's lines; one that lists its lines but no amount takes out those units and their own prices (no money without prices); a refund of 0 takes nothing off; no money comes off an order that has no value; an order both cancelled and refunded counts once; a cancel or refund of an order that was not read (placed before the window) changes nothing. **The correction has its own flag, never the read's completeness** (`returnsState`): `whole` (both read whole, and each found its order or every order of the window was read), `partial` (a read cut short, a record skipped, or one left unmatched while the orders were cut), `unread` (Klaviyo answered neither, or no time); the numbers are netted with what matched. **Catalog:** `salesFrom` counts no units of an order taken out and fewer of one partly refunded, so the units sold in 30 and 90 days, the bestseller ranks and the featured top 20 (and lane A's `listCatalog`, `assemblyProducts` and `StrategyData` products, unchanged) leave them out; a product whose orders all came back keeps its own sales (none) and never takes another product's by its title; the catalog summary's `window` stores the flag with its counts (`returns`, `cancelled`, `refunded`, `unmatched`) when the store has the metrics, and the read's log says them; the catalog's `complete`, which retires the products not seen, never depends on these reads. **Historian:** ONB-ORD part b. Ordered Product is read by neither agent (units come from the Placed Order's own lines), so nothing is taken off it. No migration (the catalog's `window` is a free object).

- INB-002b (2026-11-20): **the inbox screenshot browser never follows a redirect**, as the designed-section browser does (DST-001). `scripts/inbox-screenshots.mjs` fetches each of the job's own addresses itself (`route.fetch({ maxRedirects: 0 })`, 20 s) and refuses any 3xx answer, so an allowed address that redirects reaches neither another host, nor a private address, nor the next step of a chain (Playwright's route sees only a redirect's first address, so `route.continue()` let Chromium follow it anywhere). The job's own origins now follow DST-001's rule too (`loadableOrigins`, imported from `scripts/section-render.mjs`): https only, loopback http for local runs and tests, never an opaque one. The email's HTML and every upload are fetched with `redirect: 'error'`, so a stored email that redirects is reported `html_unreadable`. What skips the route guard is made inert before the page is drawn: `prepareHtml` turns every `<link>`, `<meta>`, `<base>`, `<iframe>`, `<frame>`, `<object>` and `<embed>` tag, wherever it is written, into an empty hidden `<wbr hidden data-gr-…>` that keeps the old attributes on it (inert with JavaScript off), so a link prefetch (which Chromium sends past `page.route`), a refresh or a moved base address never goes anywhere; the earlier whole-tag patterns missed a tag whose attribute holds a `<` (found in review: `<link rel=prefetch href="…?<">`, an upper-case tag over several lines, a link inside SVG). Every navigation is aborted as before. The run's printed counts add how many of the job's own pictures or styles were refused or failed (`Stored pictures or styles refused or failed: N.`, counts only), so a storage that starts redirecting shows up instead of silently dropping every picture. The times are options (`timing`: 20 s a picture or style, 30 s a page), and a route answered after its page closed is dropped quietly (no unhandled rejection).

(2) **Intake** (`features/email-uploads/intake.ts addUploadFile`): `readDesignFile` (`features/email-import/parse.ts`, new) applies the existing safe intake rules (no binary or container by its first bytes, no mailbox, every charset decodable, PostalMime's limits, a saved message named .html refused) but keeps the design whole up to 2,000,000 characters (the measuring browser's limit) and HTML only (a text-only email is refused: "words only, no design"); an .eml's related parts come with it. `prepareUpload` (`prepare.ts`) reads every `<img>` once: a `data:` picture or an .eml `cid:` part from the file itself; a web picture **only** from the fixed list `uploadPhotoOrigins` (`photos.ts`: `cdn.shopify.com`, Klaviyo's `d3k81ch9hvuctc.cloudfront.net`, Mailchimp's `mcusercontent.com`, `gallery.mailchimp.com` and `cdn-images.mailchimp.com`; constants, never a host the file names; our own storage left out) through `loadPicture` (moved out of `photoTools`, the same rules: every address checked with `lib/reserved-address.ts`, https only, no redirect, 8 MB, type by its first bytes, size from its header, 40 million pixels), 4 at a time within 40 s in all; anything else is listed in `missing` (site, count, why). Each picture read becomes an empty SVG of its own size with its placeholder `https://email-uploads.invalid/<n>.<ext>` beside it (`data-de-src`, our own mark), so the browser lays it out exactly and loads nothing; the HTML is marked by the inbox splitter first (the file's own marks removed). **Own design**: its pictures are kept (at most 40, 3 MiB each, 24 MiB in all). **Another brand's email**: nothing of its pictures is kept (rule 8), only their sizes for the layout. (3) **Storage** (migration `090102`): `email_uploads` (members of the workspace read their own, nobody else, operators included; written only by its commands), private bucket `email-uploads` (4 MiB; HTML, rfc822, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP; no storage policy) at `<workspace>/<upload>/original.<html|eml>` (exactly as uploaded), `email.html` (prepared) and `picture-<n>.<ext>`, written by the server's key, never over a stored file. `add_email_upload` (owner or admin of an active workspace, tenant lock; the same request key with the same file gives back the same upload, another file is refused `upload_request_used`; 100 per workspace, 20 an hour; pictures validated, none for another brand), `finish_email_upload` (every file stored at its path and size, each picture's tag pinned, then queued once), `delete_email_upload` (the row goes and its waiting job is done; the server removes the folder). A ready blueprint of another brand's email must be bare (`private.blueprint_is_bare`, the inbox's rule). (4) **The measuring job** (kind `design.upload`; `claim_email_upload` with a 5-minute lease, a paused workspace's waits an hour; `record_email_upload` once; `release_email_upload` for another engine version; a job failed four times fails its upload `measure_job_failed`): `/api/internal/design/uploads` (CRON_SECRET; GET `?peek=1`, `?engine=` claims one: its prepared HTML as a 10-minute signed link, its kind and picture count; nothing with the switch off; POST records, 600 kB), `scripts/design-uploads.mjs` in the design copies workflow (after the copies, also when they failed; counts only in the log), `features/email-uploads/measure.ts measureUpload` (JavaScript off, no request at all, our marks trusted): another brand's blueprint `forStorage` (no picture, no link); an own design's keeps its links and its stored pictures' placeholders (a placeholder past its stored pictures, or a picture not on https, becomes none). The app checks the blueprint again for the upload's kind read from the job (`finishUpload`); a table refusal is stored as `not_bare`/`not_valid`. (5) **Leak check** (`leaks.ts`, follow-up from #664's review): `hiddenMarks` flags, as kind `hidden`, any named character the engine does not write (`Ac&zz;me`, `&hearts;`; `&rarr;` joins the known table for the blocks' "Shop now →") and any invisible character (U+200B–U+200D, U+2060, U+FEFF, the soft hyphen) as a character or written as a number or a name. **Review round (26 Nov, code-review skill)**: the marks are read as a browser reads them (numbers with leading zeros or no semicolon, `&shy` without its semicolon, every format character `\p{Cf}` plus the combining grapheme joiner and the Hangul fillers; a name of the table only, never an object's own such as `&constructor;`, in `decode` too); an invisible character is flagged only where it splits a word (a letter or digit on both sides), never inside an emoji (🏳️‍🌈) nor in a word that is the brand's own; `decode` and `wordsIn` read a word an invisible character splits whole, in the copy and the source. The intake refuses a retry whose pictures changed (`upload_changed`), removes the files it wrote when the upload was deleted meanwhile, removes C1 controls from names; a blueprint's size is counted in bytes (500,000, the report body 2 MB); the stored original must have the admitted size. **Second review round (27 Nov, code-reviewer and rls-migration-reviewer on #674 at `ee8dbe8`)**: renumbered `090102` (#673 took `090100` and `090101`). (a) **Limits**: every add is kept in the append-only `email_upload_adds` (written by `add_email_upload` under the workspace lock, never touched by a delete), so the 20-an-hour limit counts add attempts; the 100 cap counts live uploads (not `deleting`, not a `saving` row left over 30 minutes); both are checked by the cheap `email_upload_room(t)` before the server reads or fetches anything (`intake.ts`), and again under the lock. (b) **Durable cleanup**: deleting makes the upload `deleting` (hidden and not counted) and cancels its waiting job; the server removes its folder, then the row (`purge_email_upload`, service role); the sweep (`sweepUploads`, GET `?sweep=1`, run by the measuring job each run) takes every `deleting` upload, makes a `saving` row left over 30 minutes `deleting`, and removes upload folders with no row for a few workspaces a run (a crashed add, a failed removal, a workspace removed). The same file added again while an earlier add of it has not finished resumes that add. (c) **Pinned files**: `finish_email_upload(t, upload, html_size)` pins `original_etag`, `html_etag` and `html_size` (the prepared HTML must be the size the server wrote) beside each picture's tag; the claim hands out `html_etag` and the app refuses a changed `email.html` (`file_changed`, the upload failed) before signing it; on a retry an `email.html` of an earlier try that differs is replaced (nothing uses an unfinished upload), pictures are compared by their SHA-256 (`samePictures`). (d) **Budgets**: 3 MB per picture for uploads (`loadPicture` `maxBytes`), 24 MB read in all, kept or not; another brand's pictures keep only their size, never their bytes; the `<img>` scan keeps each address once (a Set) and stops at the cap (30,000 tags in well under a second). (e) **Pictures in the file**: the type from the first bytes (`sniffType`; an `application/octet-stream` or `image/jpg` part works), whitespace removed from base64 `data:` pictures, a reason in the file's own words (never the web-host one). (f) **Hidden marks**: `&shy; &zwnj; &zwj; &zwsp; &nobreak; &lrm; &rlm;` go through the same split-a-word and brand-vocabulary test as the characters (the blocks' preheader padding `&#847;&zwnj;&nbsp;` passes, `Sommer&shy;schluss` with the word passes); the variation selectors (U+FE00–FE0F, U+E0100–E01EF) and the Mongolian ones (U+180B–180D) are invisible too (`Fern︎hill Deals` is caught); an apostrophe is part of the word (`Ma­ry's` with `mary's` passes). (g) **Operators** read every upload (`private.is_operator()`, as `email_copies`), since a failed `design.upload` job opens an ops task; they add, finish and delete none. (h) Waiting jobs of an upload that goes are `cancelled`; machine codes are in `hint` in every command here (as `create_email_build`); the idempotent add also compares the size and kind; `pictures` and `missing` elements are shape-checked; the peek counts only active workspaces' jobs (`email_upload_jobs_waiting`) plus uploads to clean; names are cut on whole letters (`Intl.Segmenter`); the measuring tool also removes marks written after a slash (`<img/data-de-src=…>`). `ENGINE_VERSION` `2026-11-26.2`.
- DES-ENGINE-003b (2026-11-27): **Create email copies one of the workspace's own uploaded emails** (owner decisions of 25 November: the brand's own design keeps everything and changes only the content; another brand's email is copied like a library email, rule 8; a section that cannot be copied is built from the closest library block and the email's page says which and why; a Klaviyo draft the owner schedules, D16, D17). Behind `DESIGN_UPLOAD_COPY=on` (with it off, Create email from an upload is refused and the design step never copies one). (1) **Engine**: `swapBrand` gains `keepLook` (the brand's own design): page, body, section, column, border and divider colours, every font, the logo, icons and the file's own pictures (its placeholders) stay; a text colour moves only as far as it takes to be readable (`palette.ts nudged`, 4.5:1, 3:1 for large words, the hue kept); the words, products (names, prices, photos in plan order), links (linked words stay linked, to the brand's pages) and code change; the menu keeps its own words; a picture with no words for when pictures are off (or only a file name) gets the brand's name; a picture that is not one of the file's own (a site GROS does not load pictures from, or not read) builds its section from a library block with the reason. `features/design-engine/look.ts lookProblems` is the **look kept** check, on the drawn copy against the original (colours, fonts, non-product pictures; library sections left out; a colour made readable accepted only where the original's could not be read). `libraryCopy` takes `keepLook`: no leak check against the brand's own email, `look` problems instead. (2) **Storage** (migration `090104`, after #679's `090103`): `email_builds.upload_id` (Copy only, never with an inspiration email), `create_email_build(…, upload)` (the workspace's own ready upload, under its lock, hint `build_upload_unknown` otherwise; six arguments, the five-argument command replaced); `email_copies.upload_id` (exactly one of it and `inbox_message_id`), `request_email_copy(…, upload)` (only the build's own upload, ready, in its own workspace). 3a follow-ups in the same migration: a retry of an unfinished add refreshes it (a sweep never takes it meanwhile); the sweep forgets adds older than a day. (3) **Wiring**: the worker reads the build's upload for its design step (`buildUpload`) and hands it to the ports; `buildReference` returns no reference for an upload build (its sections are planned as for Scratch, the coded email it falls back to); `libraryStep` with `uploadId` reads the upload's state (`uploadBlueprint`: waiting while it is being read, unusable when gone or failed), asks for its copy (`copyUpload`, the input with `keepLook` for an own design and no other brand's names) and refuses an own design whose look was not kept (`library_look`) or another brand's with a leak; `builtEmail.library.upload` says which. The copy job hands out the upload's blueprint and prepared HTML (only while its HTML is the one pinned) and the script passes `keepLook`; `finishCopy`'s leak check reads the upload's kind itself (never the copy's input): another brand's is checked against its prepared HTML, the brand's own is not. A done own-design copy's pictures (each still the one pinned when it was added, its tag and size) are signed for 30 days in place of their placeholders (`uploadPictureLinks`), so the push imports them into Klaviyo (rule 11). (4) **Screens**: "Use this design" on a ready upload (owner) opens `/inspiration/use?upload=<id>` (the preview of the prepared HTML, an own design's pictures at signed links; no Copy/Remix choice, one line on what GROS does) and Create email (`createEmailFromUpload`); the email's page ("The design you chose") says "Your own design was kept…" or "copied from the email you added…", then each section built differently and why. The export routes stay. 3a follow-ups in the app: a stored prepared HTML of another size is never replaced on a resume (`upload_changed`); the measuring script refuses a downloaded HTML whose tag is not the pinned one; a web picture refused as over 3 MB counts the bytes read against the 24 MB budget. `ENGINE_VERSION` `2026-11-27.1`.
