## Migration allocation

To reduce parallel conflicts, each workstream owns a numeric migration block. Do not renumber an already shared migration.

| Range            | Owner                                |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `2026091400xxxx` | Foundation/extensions/helpers        |
| `2026091401xxxx` | Identity/tenancy/RLS                 |
| `2026091402xxxx` | Brand/AI/prompts/usage               |
| `2026091403xxxx` | Integrations/jobs/Klaviyo/Shopify    |
| `2026091404xxxx` | Campaigns/calendar/audiences         |
| `2026091405xxxx` | References/competitors/templates     |
| `2026091406xxxx` | Designers/submissions                |
| `2026091407xxxx` | Support/feedback/notifications       |
| `2026091408xxxx` | Packages/reporting/admin additions   |
| `2026091409xxxx` | Integration fixes/materialized views |

New migrations after the hosted project reached `20260914090016` use the next `2026091409xxxx` number, whatever their domain. Since 2026-11-06 the Supabase GitHub integration applies every migration merged to `main` to the live database, and the hosted project refuses out-of-order versions. **Since 2026-11-11 (D24) there are no reservations:** right before merging, rename an unmerged migration to the next number after the newest on `main`, then re-run `test:db`. On `main`: `090017` (UIR-013 connection profiles), `090018`–`090019` (UIR-005 brand profile sections and facts), `090020`–`090021` (UIR-011 Settings), `090022`–`090023` (UIR-012 Holidays), `090024`–`090025` (UIR-019 Team), `090026`–`090027` (UIR-020 Feature Requests), `090028`–`090030` (UIR-023 brand timezone), `090031`–`090032` (UIR-021 brand-mismatch guard), `090033`–`090034` (UIR-009 Inspiration), `090038`–`090039` (INB-001 inbox), `090040` (INB-002 images and screenshots), `090043` (INB-003 sections and facts), `090044`–`090045` (INB-004 ops queue and brand directory), `090046` (GEM-002 live AI usage), `090047` (GEM-003 platform AI budget), `090048` (MEM-001 agent memory), `090049` (KLV-001 live Klaviyo), `090050` (CI-001 competitor tags), `090051` (RET-002 agent fallbacks), `090052` (CI-002 block variants), `090054` (DSC-001 max discount and discount codes), `090055` (ONB-101 brand findings), `090056` (STR-003 part 2 strategy runs), `090057` (ONB-102 catalog reading), `090058` (EML-004 part 2 email builds), `090059` (ONB-103 Klaviyo history; numbered at merge time). `090035`–`090036` (UIR-008 Ask GROS, parked) are older than `main` and must be renumbered before they merge.

Use a valid 14-digit Supabase migration version inside the assigned UTC-hour namespace, for example `20260914010000_create_tenants.sql`, then increment seconds monotonically. The namespace is an ordering device, not a claim about wall-clock creation time.

## Release checklist

- [ ] Database resets from zero with migrations and safe seed.
- [ ] Generated Supabase types match the final schema.
- [ ] Typecheck, lint, unit, integration, RLS, and Playwright suites pass.
- [ ] Client/admin/designer authorization is deny-by-default.
- [ ] Two-tenant negative-access suite passes.
- [ ] Service-role key never appears in a client bundle.
- [ ] External credentials are encrypted or held only in platform secrets.
- [ ] Queue consumers use leases, attempts, idempotency keys, and dead-letter behavior.
- [ ] Cron endpoints validate a secret and do not trust public callers.
- [ ] AI usage checks run before provider dispatch and reconcile actual usage afterward.
- [ ] File buckets and signed URLs enforce tenant/assignment access.
- [ ] Security headers and rate limits are enabled.
- [ ] Production contains no demo passwords or destructive seed behavior.
- [ ] Preview smoke test completes the P0 campaign journey.
- [ ] Rollback and operational runbooks are documented.

The exact CI sequences were run locally on the lean stack: fresh reset → `pnpm test:db` 600/600; fresh reset → full `pnpm test:e2e` 80/80 (STAB-001 run); fresh reset → `test-first-draft`, `test-email-concurrency`, `test-email-import-concurrency` all passed. - Review: `code-reviewer` found nothing blocking. The browser job no longer runs on push to `main`, so a broken merge result between two green pull requests would only be caught by `verify` or the next pull request.
- Owner update: Actions was enabled on November 6, 2026; at the owner's request this PR also moves the scheduled-jobs workflow to every 30 minutes and updates both runbooks.

- Changed contracts: new service-role-only RPCs `public.reserve_ai_usage(t, operation, feature, estimate)` and `public.settle_ai_usage(t, reservation, actual)`: `ai:` operations only, one reservation per operation (a second reserve is `PT409`), `expires_at = infinity` so an unsettled live call keeps counting until ops settles it. `reserve_fixture_usage` / `reconcile_fixture_usage` now refuse `ai:` operations (as they already refused `email-rewrite:`). `private.reserve_budget` treats `ai:` as live for the cap message and the 80% alert ("real AI requests"). - Migrations: `20260914090046_live_ai_usage.sql`.
- Verification run: `vitest run features/ai` 19/19; eslint and tsc clean for `features/ai`. `supabase/tests/live_ai_usage.test.sql` (owner, foreign owner and no-role callers can't reserve, settle, release or pre-seed live usage; the expiry sweep leaves live rows alone; double reserve is PT409; over-estimate settle 23514; second different settle PT409; the stale sweep charges the estimate; privileges). rls-migration-reviewer findings fixed: stray statement fragment, ambiguous `id`, duplicate check now under the tenant lock could not run here (no Docker); CI's Supabase job runs it.

Many review apps publish no photos in their review data at all; those stores keep none. A store whose product pictures are on its own domain (`/cdn/shop/`) proves no Shopify CDN folder, so its review photos on `cdn.shopify.com` are left out. The database refuses a read with Shopify CDN photos in two folders, or Judge.me photos in two, but cannot tell whether the one folder is the store's (only the reader checks it): an accepted limit. A word of the reviewer's name in a photo's address leaves it out, even when it is a product word ("Rose" and "rose-scarf.jpg"). Only the first 100 reviews with a photo on a page are looked at. The HTML parser itself is slow on markup nested tens of thousands deep (as the Site reader). Photos of a review cut by the 5-quote cap are still kept (the review passes part b's rules). Nothing in "Create email" uses them yet.

Real Chromium (`tests/e2e/inbox-render.spec.ts`, the new INB-002b test: the job's own server redirects to another host, to a private address (127.0.0.2 stands in) and along a chain, from an image, a background, an `@import` and an entity-written meta refresh; neither the other host nor the private one gets a request, the chain stops at its first step, the picture is still taken); it failed before the change (the chain reached `/chain-2.png`). `section-render.spec.ts` still passes. The scheduled sweep journey on an isolated local stack took the inbox screenshot through the new guard (taken, none failed, 600 to 640 px). After the review (`main` merged in, with CI-007): unit tests (every `<link>`, `<meta>` and `<base>` made inert however written, `<metadata>` and text left alone; `fulfill` gets the fetched answer; the printed counts); real Chromium: each redirecting address asked exactly once, the refresh never sent, the five refused counted, and the job's own red picture drawn in the screenshot; the three `<link>` shapes the review found, a preconnect, a refresh and a `<base>`: the outside server gets no request (with the old patterns it got `/pf?%3C`, `/pf-upper` and `/pf-svg?%3C`); with 300 ms and 1 s times, a picture that never answers is dropped and the email still photographed, and a page whose style chain outlasts its time is reported `render_failed` while the run photographs the next one, with no unhandled rejection after the page closed. A second loopback address (127.0.0.2) stands in for a private one; where there is none (macOS), localhost does.

Its should-fix applied: the inert tags (`<link`, `<meta`, `<base`) become an empty hidden `<wbr hidden data-gr-…>` instead of an unknown `<gr-…>` tag, which wrapped everything after it, so `body > table` rules stopped matching and a screenshot lost the email's own layout (e2e "an email keeps its own layout once its head tags are made inert", which fails with the old renaming: the table's parent was `GR-LINK`). Charset is unaffected: the email's text is decoded when it arrives and stored as UTF-8 (checked with windows-1252, iso-8859-1, shift_jis and utf-8 metas).

### 2026-11-11 — MEM-002 — thinking room on Gemini 2.5 calls

- Status: review
- Branch/worktree: `claude/mem-002-thinking-room`
- Commit(s): see the MEM-002 pull request.
- Changed contracts: `AiProviderRequest.maxOutputTokens` now means the room for the answer. For Gemini 2.5 with a `reasoningEffort`, the provider adds the thinking budget on top (`geminiOutputTokens`: low +1,024, medium +4,096; capped at 65,536), because 2.5 counts thinking as output and a cut-off inside the thinking came back as `incomplete` (no answer, no retry). The cost reservation in `runAi` uses the same number. 2.5 Pro never gets a budget below 128 (it cannot switch thinking off). Agents keep `maxOutputTokens` at the answer size; lane A's `outputLimit` (EML-001) can go back to the answer size only.
- Migrations: none.
- Verification run: `vitest run lib/providers features/ai features/agents features/strategy features/intelligence` (176 pass); eslint and tsc clean for the changed files.
- Models that decide their own thinking (any 3.x model, and 2.5 Flash or Pro with no `reasoningEffort`) get a fixed 4,096 tokens of thinking room on top of the answer; 2.5 Flash-Lite with no effort does not think and gets none. The total never exceeds 65,536, so an answer room near that cap is trimmed.
- Known issues: none.
- Next consumer: lanes A and B (every AgentDefinition).

### 2026-11-17 — DST-004b1 — the match score in code

- Status: review
- Branch/worktree: `claude/dst-004b1-match-score`, from `main` after DST-002c1 (#602).
- Commit(s): see the DST-004b1 pull request.
- Changed contracts: see Global decision DST-004b1. New `features/studio/match.ts` (`LumaGrid`, `gridProblem`, `resample`, `layoutShare`, `matchScore`, `isMatchScore`, `matchColumns`, `matchTarget`, `maxGridSide`, `withMatch`); `StudioPorts.match?`, its use in `studioRound` and the coded reason `match_failed` (`features/studio/rounds.ts`).
- Migrations: none.
- Verification run: `pnpm verify`; `match.test.ts` (13: the same picture scores 10, also drawn larger or 20% taller; the brand’s own textured photo in the same place, 30%, 50% and 70% wide, at the target or more; a smooth full-bleed photo (12 seeded pairs), with its headline over it or not, at the target or more; a photo filling a section whose reference has a flat background, and the other way round, below it; content at the other end at the same brightness, the photo on the other side, the tones turned round and a busy picture for a plain one below it; only whole scores 1 to 10; area-weighted resampling; grids it cannot read, and a throw for one; a whole score for any two grids; the verdict at the target, below it with the problem, the critic’s own problems first; the smooth and filled tests fail on the round-2 score); `rounds.test.ts` (+6: a Copy section that looks like its reference is taken; one that does not is designed again, told how to come closer; a match that cannot be measured, a port that throws and a number that is not a score leave the critic’s verdict without asking the critic again; Scratch, Remix, a Copy brief without a reference and no port are never measured; a Copy section still too unlike after its last round is coded `match_failed`). Experiments on painted 120×120 grids, the reviewer’s scripts run by the author on the final score: the same layout with the brand’s own photo, 29 pairs each, passes for smooth (one to three waves) photos 60% wide, for smooth full-bleed photos and for smooth full-bleed photos under a headline; a light smooth product photo on a light background 3 to 9 (17 of 29 pass); a full-bleed photo against a half-photo reference 4; a soft gradient background drawn for a flat one 4; the photo on the other side 4 (7 when a full-height photo is 70% wide, where the two overlap); light and dark turned round 1; a plain white picture 1; the words left out 8. Reviewed by code-reviewer: round 1 not ready (SSIM measured the inside of the photo, so a faithful rebuild with the brand’s own large photo scored 1 to 6; also a match failure logged as the critic’s, a throwing port paying for the critic again, numbers that are not scores, tests that could not see the photo); round 2 not ready (a smooth full-bleed photo still scored 1 to 7, the test used only a blocky photo; the ledger credited the experiments to the reviewer); both fixed here with the reviewer’s direction (a flat background within 2 levels, a filled picture content everywhere) and a penalty for a flat background against a filled one, which keeps a full-bleed photo from passing for a half-photo layout.
- Known issues: nothing gives the `match` port its grids yet (part 4b2: the drawn section’s grid from the render job, the reference section’s from the inbox screenshots or a decoder), so today nothing is measured and the critic decides alone. The Section designer sees only the reference section’s tone and height, not its picture or layout, so a round told to come closer has little to go on (part 4b2 should give it the reference’s layout). The target (6) and the levels (26 for content, 2 for a flat background, a quarter of the cells, 0.6 for a flat background against a filled one) are first values, tuned on painted grids, to be tuned with the design proof (AGENT_MAP: five inbox emails rebuilt and shown with their match scores). Known weak cases: a light product photo on a light background reads partly as background (3 to 9 for a faithful rebuild); a full-height photo moved to the other side still scores 7 when it is 70% wide; a soft gradient background where the reference is flat scores 4; the words count little (left out, 8; the critic requires the headline); when neither picture has a flat background (a photo fills both) every cell is content, so the score is always 10 and only the critic judges the layout (the headline at the other edge passes); a reference whose background is not flat (paper-like, softly shaded) against a faithful flat rebuild scores 4, the mirror of the gradient case. Part 4b2’s grids must be area-averaged (each cell the mean of the pixels it covers): a flat background stays within 2 levels only so, and sampling one pixel per cell would read noise as content. A match that could not be measured leaves no trace (the section passes on the critic alone, unlogged), and the score is not saved with the section yet (the design proof needs both).
- Next consumer: DST-004b2 (the grids), the design proof.

New `features/design-engine/` (`blueprint.ts`, `measurement.ts`, `measure.ts`, `roles.ts`, `fonts.ts`, `render.ts`, `likeness.ts`, `content.ts`, `fallback.ts`, `copy.ts`, `browser.ts`, `fixtures.ts`, and `golden/` with the 40 emails, their plain-colour pictures and the report writer). New `lib/sandbox/browser.mjs` (+ `.d.mts`): the locked browser's shared rules, `loadableOrigins`, `makeInert` and `launch` (Chromium with no secret in its environment and its OS sandbox first), moved out of `scripts/section-render.mjs` and `scripts/inbox-screenshots.mjs`, which import and re-export them unchanged. `features/blocks/render.ts` exports `blockMobileCss`. New workflow `.github/workflows/design-engine.yml` (pull requests and pushes to main touching the engine, the blocks, the inbox splitter or `lib/sandbox`; by hand): installs Chromium, runs `vitest run features/design-engine` with `DESIGN_ENGINE_BROWSER=on` and always uploads `design-golden/` (results.json, summary.md, index.html and one side-by-side picture per email: original, redraw, redraw at 375 px, both as grey boxes). `.gitignore` and `.prettierignore` skip `design-golden/`. No new dependency: Playwright (already a dev dependency), parse5 (the inbox splitter) and node:zlib (the test pictures).
- Migrations: none.
- Limits (each a plain `{ ok: false }` reason, never a crash or a wait without end): an email over 2 MB, a page taller than 16,000 px (read through the browser's own page metrics), a snapshot of more than 30,000 parts, a snapshot over 15 s, a whole measurement over 30 s (`browserLimits`); an attribute longer than a blueprint keeps (an inline picture over 200,000 characters, anything else over 4,000) is dropped, never cut; a picture held at its size only up to 2,000 × 16,000 px; the owner's pictures cut at 6,000 px and 3 MB. `copyDesign` never throws: a timeout, a page trying to navigate, a refused drawing and anything unexpected come back as `{ ok: false, error }`. Klaviyo mode needs the real brand (`copyDesign` and `drawBlueprint` refuse without it); a preview reads the colours from the email, with no made-up store link and no made-up button words. `drawBlueprint` checks the blueprint against the schema first; font names hold no quotes, semicolons or brackets; inline pictures are PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP only. Uploaded HTML loses any `data-gr-section` or `data-de-*` marks it brings and is cut by the inbox splitter; only our own marks are trusted (`trustMarks`: a redraw, later a stored inbox email).
- Verification run: `pnpm verify` (format, lint, typecheck, unit tests, build). Fast unit tests without a browser: `blueprint.test.ts`, `measure.test.ts` (a made-up measured email: sections, fills, roles, runs, button, cards, an unsupported timer, the snapshot reader, attributes over the limit), `render.test.ts` (schema first, Klaviyo needs the brand), `likeness.test.ts` (every limit on both sides of its edge, dividers at 1 px, grey-box scores, phone problems), `content.test.ts`, `fonts.test.ts`, `fallback.test.ts`, `browser.test.ts` (marks, `$` patterns, sizes no email has, 2 MB), `lib/sandbox/browser.test.ts`, and `tests/ci/workflows.test.ts` (+1). In the browser (`DESIGN_ENGINE_BROWSER=on`, Chromium launched with `launch`, run locally and in the new workflow): the golden set **40 of 40** pass the likeness check **and** the content unchanged check (gate: 36); `engine.browser.test.ts` (a countdown-timer section built from the Offer banner block with its reason; a moving picture with no words left out and every later section still copied; a section that keeps failing drawn twice more, corrected, then built from the closest block with "still differed from the original after 3 tries (…)"; a dropped link and a wrong colour fail the content check while every size is right; Klaviyo without the brand, a picture not uploaded and a measurement out of time come back as plain reasons; a column 10 px narrower is caught; a fixed-width email that overflows a phone is redrawn to stack cleanly; an upload's own section marks are ignored); `sandbox.browser.test.ts` (two loopback servers: only the allowed origin's named addresses are fetched; a redirect out and a redirect to another path on the allowed origin are not followed; a sizeless outside picture, CSS `url()`, `@import`, `<link>`, a script (JavaScript off, it never runs) and a meta refresh reach nothing; a picture that never answers and a measurement out of time; the height, part and size limits; the owner's picture cut at 6,000 px).
- **Live switch:** none. Nothing calls the engine yet; no AI (paid or fake) measures or draws.
- Tolerances as coded (`likeness.ts limits`): the same sections in number, kind and order; columns within 2 px of their width and place; each section within 5 % of its height, at least 2 px (max(2 px, 5 %)); text sizes, buttons, pictures and dividers within 1 px; picture shapes within 2 %; grey-box layouts at least 0.9 alike (4 px cells); nothing past the screen or a picture under something else at 375 px. Content unchanged (`content.ts`, only for a copy that keeps the source's content, `keepContent`, true in step 1): words and line breaks, bold, italic, colours, sizes, underlines and links of every run; text colour, alignment, font list (the drawn one starts with the original's), weight, italics, capitals and letter spacing; picture address, alt text and link; button words, link, colours, border and font; divider colour; column and section fills, borders and corners; the colours around the email.

A failing section whose parts differ (not only its sizes) goes to the library block after one drawing, since a correction cannot change its parts. Not kept from a source yet: `<sup>`/`<sub>` (drawn on the line), list bullets drawn by CSS (bullets typed as characters are kept), words over a background picture or gradient (built from a block), a section's own rounded corners, and different borders per side (one border is kept). A blank line between two lines of words in a legacy `<font>` email is kept by sharing the measured height evenly. A picture the browser may not load and that has no width and height attributes is measured as its alt text; an http picture is kept as its box only (a blueprint keeps https pictures). A link longer than 2,000 characters is dropped (its words stay); more than 12 columns side by side or more than 200 parts in one place make the section one that cannot be copied. On a machine that cannot give Chromium its OS sandbox (some containers), `launch` falls back to launching without it, as the inbox job does. Phone layout: columns stack, side margins shrink to 16 px, narrow centred sections stay centred; rows of icons or a menu stay side by side. The draw is checked in Chromium only; real Outlook and Gmail previews are step 5.
